Companion to 00-overview, 01-event-bus, 02-chaser-header, 03-chaser-download, 04-chaser-validate. chaser_confirm is the only writer to the confirmed chain. It takes the validated portion of the candidate chain (heights from the current confirmed top up to where validation, bypass or prior confirmation guarantees acceptance) and: compares branch work against the current confirmed branch, reorganises the confirmed chain (pop ⇒ push) if the candidate is stronger, runs query.block_confirmable(link) per block to do the order-based consensus checks against the now-committed confirmed chain, persists block_confirmable and the filter head, and pushes the confirmed link, emits chase::confirmable / chase::unconfirmable per block, chase::organized / chase::reorganized per push/pop, chase::block when announcing newly-confirmed blocks to peers, and chase::stale when the confirmed chain ages out of the currency window. The full transition from "header arrived" to "confirmed in the chain" goes: chaser_header → chaser_download → chaser_validate → chaser_confirm (organize) (download) (consensus) (order + commit) Confirmation is sequential and not cancellable — unlike validate's parallel pool. File Role include/bitcoin/node/chasers/chaser_confirm.hpp Class declaration src/chasers/chaser_confirm.cpp Implementation
There is no longer a defer-confirmation setting: the chaser always subscribes (chaser_confirm.cpp:43-58). Its only configuration input is the currency window used by the stale timer (§7).

chaser_confirm runs on its own chaser strand on the network pool; no override. Confirmation cannot be parallelised because each block depends on the cumulative state of the chain up to its parent — strictly sequential. Invariant (Confirm-Conc-1). All confirm operations run on the chaser's own strand. Every do_* and helper has BC_ASSERT(stranded()) at entry. No off-strand work.

The chaser holds no in-memory state machine state beyond the base class's position_ (set in start, otherwise unused) and the stale timer (chaser_confirm.hpp:78). All durable state lives in the database, specifically: Method Effect on store query.push_confirmed(link, !under_checkpoint) Add to confirmed chain (strong = !under_checkpoint) query.pop_confirmed() Remove top of confirmed chain query.set_block_confirmable(link) Mark block as confirmed-in-chain (state transition) query.set_block_unconfirmable(link) Mark block as permanently rejected query.set_filter_head(link) Commit BIP158 filter head record Invariant (Confirm-Store-1). chaser_confirm and chaser_header are the only writers to the candidate / confirmed chain order. chaser_confirm is the only writer to the confirmed projection (push_confirmed / pop_confirmed); the header chaser only touches candidate. This separation underpins the spec's two-projection view.

Inputs: Event Source Reaction chase::start full_node do_bump → do_bumped chase::resume full_node do_bump chase::bump chaser_header, chaser_validate, or self do_bump chase::valid chaser_validate do_validated(h) → do_bumped chase::regressed/disorganized chaser_header do_regressed(h) — no-op (only BC_ASSERT(stranded())) chase::stop service unsubscribe Suspension: handle_chase short-circuits with return true if suspended() (chaser_confirm.cpp:84-85). do_bumped also has an explicit early exit on suspended() (:158-159). Invariant (Confirm-Regress-1). Regression events are not acted upon. The next bump-driven call to do_bumped will use query.get_validated_fork against the current candidate chain, which reflects the regression. So the chaser naturally tracks rollbacks without explicit handling. Outputs (all from chaser_confirm.cpp, all stranded): Event Site Payload Trigger chase::reorganized :380 (in set_reorganized) link Each pop_confirmed during a reorg or rollback chase::organized :413 (in set_organized) link Each push_confirmed during a reorg or rollback chase::block :445 (in announce) link Each set_organized if the confirmed chain is current chase::stale :482 (in handle_stale_timer) — The confirmed top aged past the currency window without a new block chase::unconfirmable :355 (in notify_block) link Block failed block_confirmable check chase::confirmable :362 (in notify_block) link Block passed, or was bypassed / previously confirmable

The fork returned by get_validated_fork is the shortest candidate chain above the fork point whose blocks are all in a confirmable state; with the database's scanned/filtered gating, a block whose silent-payment or filter indexing is still banked is not yet part of it (doc 04 §5.4).
organize (chaser_confirm.cpp:240-291) is a switch on the candidate-side state flags of each block in the fork, read with the database's is_bypass, is_confirmable, is_validated predicates:

// chaser_confirm.cpp:253-262 if (!query.set_filter_head(item.link)) { fault(confirm6); return; } complete_block(error::success, item.link, height, true); // bypass=true A block previously marked as bypass (under checkpoint or milestone in validate). Skip confirmation work, just persist filter head, mark "confirmed" (via set_organized below).

// chaser_confirm.cpp:263-267 // Previously confirmable is not considered bypass. complete_block(error::success, item.link, height, false); Already confirmed (e.g. during a prior session, or on a branch that was popped and is now being restored). Just emit chase::confirmable and continue; push_confirmed re-establishes its position.

The normal path — block was validated, must now be confirmed against the current confirmed chain. // chaser_confirm.cpp:293-330 (confirm_block) if (const auto ec = query.block_confirmable(link)) { if (!query.set_block_unconfirmable(link)) { fault(confirm9); return false; } if (!roll_back(popped, fork_point, height-1)) { fault(confirm10); return false; } return complete_block(ec, link, height, false); // emits chase::unconfirmable } if (!query.set_filter_head(link)) { fault(confirm11); return false; } if (!query.set_block_confirmable(link)) { fault(confirm12); return false; } return complete_block(error::success, link, height, false); // emits chase::confirmable Invariant (Confirm-Order-1). set_filter_head precedes set_block_confirmable. Symmetric with validate's ordering: state bit is the last write so it never advances over an incomplete record. Invariant (Confirm-Rollback-1). A block_confirmable failure triggers roll_back(popped, fork_point, height-1) which: 1. Pops the confirmed top back to fork_point (reversing confirmations completed for this fork before the failing block). 2. Re-pushes the originally-popped blocks (restoring the previous confirmed chain). Implementation: chaser_confirm.cpp:422-436. Post-condition: confirmed chain == its state before this do_bumped call.

// chaser_confirm.cpp:274-278 default: fault(error::confirm7); Invariant (Confirm-State-1). get_validated_fork should not include blocks that are unassociated, unvalidated, or unconfirmable. If it does, the store is inconsistent and the chaser faults — proof obligation for libbitcoin-database.

complete_block (:333-347) treats any database-category error from block_confirmable as a fault (:339-344) — disk full is the recoverable case — and otherwise hands the code to notify_block, which emits unconfirmable for a consensus failure or confirmable for success (:349-366).

set_organized calls announce (:417), which emits chase::block and (re)starts the stale timer only when the confirmed chain is current (:438-448). The timer expires at the top block's timestamp plus the currency window, which may be sooner than a full window from now (:452-466); on expiry it emits chase::stale (:469-483). Each new current block restarts it. Consumers: session_outbound adjusts its connection count on both events, protocol_transaction_out_70013 re-sends its fee filter (the maximum while stale), and the header/block out protocols and chaser_snapshot / chaser_estimate act on block (doc 01 §2.6). Invariant (Confirm-Announce-1). chase::block(link) is emitted only when is_current_chain(true). Peers don't get announcements for catch-up blocks. Invariant (Confirm-Stale-1). Between a chase::block and the next one, at most one chase::stale is emitted, and only after the top's timestamp plus the currency window has passed. A zero window disables the timer (:457-458).

Confirmed monotonicity (modulo reorgs): after each successful set_organized, top_confirmed increases by exactly one. After each successful set_reorganized, it decreases by exactly one. Reorg atomicity (Confirm-Rollback-1): if confirm_block fails mid-fork, the post-rollback state equals the pre-do_bumped state. Either the whole fork commits or no part of it does. State-bit ordering (Confirm-Order-1): set_block_confirmable is the last write per block. A reader observing the confirmable flag is guaranteed that set_filter_head and (eventually) push_confirmed have completed. Work monotonicity at switch (get_strong_fork with ties accepted): the confirmed chain only changes when the candidate's work above the fork point is at least the confirmed work above it. A tie can only arise from prioritization (doc 02 §6.4). Bypassed soundness: blocks confirmed in bypass mode were previously gated by is_under_checkpoint(height) ∨ query.is_milestone(link) in validate — a checkpoint/milestone is the upstream proof of consensus correctness, transitively used here.

Provided validate keeps emitting chase::valid, every block on the candidate chain with a validated state eventually receives a do_bumped call that includes it in the fork. The self-bump after fork drain (chaser_confirm.cpp:288-290) ensures no stall when chase::valid arrived during the in-progress iteration.

This is a significant consensus operation, not a narrow double-spend probe. It evaluates all block-relative, order-based consensus constraints on a block — everything except header chaining and the chain-summation rules (cumulative work, MTP). Specifically: Strong-tx association for every spent prevout. For every input, the previous output must be in a strong transaction — i.e. a tx that is associated to a block which is either (a) confirmed, or (b) in the confirmable candidate fork at lesser height than the spending block. This is the property that subsumes the "is the prevout in the UTXO set?" question, expressed in a tx→block association model rather than a separate UTXO snapshot. Coinbase maturity (100-confirmation rule for spending coinbase outputs). Relative locktime rules (BIP68 sequence locks). These checks also exist on the system::chain objects (for completeness, e.g. for stand-alone validation tools), but driving them there requires populating each input's metadata first. The store optimizes by performing the queries that would have populated that metadata, directly — much more efficient than populate-then-check. Validation persists prevout metadata (set_prevouts, doc 04 §4.3) specifically to make this query fast. So block_confirmable is correctly read as: "under the assumption that all lower-height blocks in this fork are confirmable, is this block consensus-valid against all order-sensitive rules?" Its correctness is the joint responsibility of the libbitcoin-database query implementation and the consensus rules it encodes; a formal model should treat the call as a non-trivial proof obligation, not a thin UTXO oracle. For a model: block_confirmable(link, fork, store_state) → Right(()) if for every input in block(link): - prevout tx is strong under (store_state ∪ fork[< height]) - coinbase maturity satisfied - relative-locktime constraints satisfied - no double-spends within fork[≤ height] Left(error_code) otherwise The chaser sequences calls so that prior fork blocks have already had set_block_confirmable written by the time block_confirmable(link) runs for this block (loop ordering at chaser_confirm.cpp:248-286).

Confirmation is sequential — a single-threaded function, with no parallelism to model. The reorg / rollback structure is a clean two-phase commit: pop-confirmed-down-to-fork-point, then push-new-tops; on per-block failure, run roll-back. The fork is returned by get_validated_fork as a list of header_state records, iterated forward. Three state arms (bypass, confirmable, validated) and one fault arm — a simple case/switch.

The entire chaser is strand-confined (Confirm-Conc-1). Single-threaded reasoning suffices. The most subtle property is the rollback: prove that if confirm_block fails at height h after j prior successful pushes in this fork, then roll_back(popped, fork_point, h-1) is equivalent to undoing those j pushes and re-pushing the original popped. The "current chain" gate on chase::block (Confirm-Announce-1) and the stale timer are purely about peer-facing currency; not safety properties.

Companion to 00-overview, 01-event-bus, 02-chaser-header. chaser_download is the dispatcher between the header chain and the peer block-download protocols. Conceptually: The header chaser commits to a candidate chain of headers. chaser_download notices which heights in that chain still lack block bodies (are unassociated) and partitions them into work-maps. Peer protocols (protocol_block_in_31800) pull maps via get_hashes, download the blocks, and return any leftovers via put_hashes. As blocks arrive (chase::checked), the position advances; when the position reaches the end of the request window it emits chase::windowed; as validation completes (chase::valid), the request window slides forward. chaser_download also runs the performance-policing loop: peers report their download speed, slow peers are detected by standard deviation, and starved peers cause work to be split off slow peers. 1.3 Why advanced_ is a counter, not a height

do_advanced (chaser_download.cpp:369-379) increments advanced_ on every chase::valid event, regardless of which height was validated. The round is complete when advanced_ == requested_. This is correct because: Every block hash that is requested will eventually be validated or the peer will fail (and the hash is returned to the pool). Once requested_ round-trips have completed, the request window can slide forward without leaving gaps below. It does not track an in-order height; out-of-order validation is permitted as long as the count balances. Invariant (Download-State-1). position() ≤ requested_ and advanced_ ≤ requested_ always hold on the strand. set_unassociated short-circuits if either falls behind (chaser_download.cpp:503-509).

job_ is a network::race_all<const code&> whose completer is handle_purged. Semantics: A race_all invokes its completer once all copies are dropped. chaser_download holds one copy in job_. Every peer protocol that calls get_hashes receives a copy via the map_handler (chaser_download.cpp:455: handler(success, get_map(), job_)). When chaser_download drops its copy via stop_tracking() (:193-201), the completer fires only after every peer has also dropped its copy — i.e., released its current download work. So job_ is effectively a purge barrier: "wait until every in-flight download has either completed or surrendered, then resume". Invariant (Download-Job-1). job_ == nullptr ⇒ chaser is purging (currently waiting for the barrier). While purging, all of do_bump, do_get_hashes, do_put_hashes, and set_unassociated are no-ops (:393-394, :452-453, :463-464, :500-501). The transition out of purging is exactly the do_handle_purged callback (:213-219) which calls start_tracking() followed by do_bump.

Invariant (Download-Purge-1). A chase::purge emission is always followed (eventually, after barrier completion) by an idempotent return to the ACTIVE state with position_ rewound to min(branch_point, position), requested_ = advanced_ = position, and maps_ empty (:348-364). While in PURGING, no work is handed out and no new work is computed. Invariant (Download-Purge-2). do_regressed ignores regressions at or above max(position, requested_) (:353-354). These are "inconsequential": neither the position nor the window has reached that height, so there is no work to purge. A regression inside the window but above the position still purges, because the window must follow the position or the gap it awaits is never requested. Invariant (Download-Window-1). chase::windowed(height) is emitted exactly when the contiguous associated position reaches the last requested height (:401-408). chaser_validate uses it to know that no more blocks are coming for the window and drain its batches (doc 04 §5).

chaser_download is the only chaser that interacts with peer connections beyond bus events: protocol_block_in_31800 calls full_node::performance(channel, speed, handler) periodically, which forwards to chaser_download::update. The reply code tells the peer whether to keep going or terminate.

speed == max_uint64: erase(channel); return exhausted_channel speed == 0: erase(channel); return stalled_channel otherwise: record speed = double(speed) if count(speeds_) < 4: return success compute mean, σ from speeds_ if speed ≥ mean: return success if (mean - speed) > α·σ: return slow_channel else: return success (chaser_download.cpp:278-343; minimum_for_standard_deviation = 4, chaser_download.hpp:83) exhausted_channel: peer announces "I have nothing else useful for you". Peer pauses its timer; the record is released. stalled_channel: peer reports zero progress. Peer drops itself. slow_channel: peer is statistically below the herd. Returned only when ≥ 4 samples and the gap exceeds allowed_deviation × σ.
6.2 do_starved (when a peer has no work)

protocol_block_in_31800 emits chase::starved(self) when it receives an empty map. do_starved (:224-253): Removes self from speeds_ (so it can't be picked as its own victim). Picks the slowest remaining channel by speeds_ min. If found: erases it and notify_one(slow, chase::split, self) — direct that single channel to split its work and stop, leaving the starved channel something to claim. If speeds_ is empty: broadcast chase::stall(self) to all download-capable channels. The receiver of split/stall is protocol_block_in_31800; see 06 §5.3.

set_unassociated (chaser_download.cpp:496-571) is the heart of work generation. It: Early-exits if purging, if not all previously-requested work has cleared (position < requested), or if validation has not caught up (advanced < requested) (:500-509). Latches inventory_ on first nonzero (:512-514 → get_inventory_size). Computes a stop height: min(position + maximum_concurrency, maximum_height), clamped to the bypass height while the position is under it (:524-527). Bypassed blocks may archive unprobed, so the window must not extend above the bypass height until all blocks at or below it are associated. When current and compact_timeout is nonzero, if the top candidate is a compact-announced header that is not yet associated, clamps stop to one below it and starts the compact timer (once per link) (:530-547). This gives the compact fill a chance before the block is downloaded in full; when the timer fires, expired_ records the link and do_headers re-runs the generator without the clamp (:573-582). Loops query.get_unassociated_above(requested_, inventory_, stop), chunking each result into a map_ptr and pushing onto maps_, until set_map returns false (empty map, end of unassociated headers below stop) (:549-560). Returns total count added. get_inventory_size (:584-593): Returns 0 if no connections OR if is_current_chain(false) is false — i.e. the candidate (header) chain isn't current. Otherwise: ceilinged_divide(unassociated_count_above(fork, step), connections). The candidate-current gate is not "wait until caught up" — issuing zero work until the node is caught up would just stall. Instead it guards against dividing work over a weak header chain: until headers are current, the partitioning of unassociated heights into per-peer inventory chunks could be meaningless, so block download is paused until header sync has produced a current (and therefore presumed near-canonical) candidate. Invariant (Download-Inventory-1). inventory_ is computed at most once (latch on first nonzero result, :512-514). Peer inventory size is fixed for the run, after the first "currentness" of the chain. Invariant (Download-Bypass-1). No download window spans the bypass height: while position < bypass_height, stop ≤ bypass_height (:526-527). Validation of bypassed blocks therefore never races ahead of their association.

Unlike chaser_header, chaser_download does not define numbered faults. Its errors are channel-class codes returned to the peer (the chaser itself does not call fault): Code returned by do_update Meaning error::exhausted_channel peer has no more work to offer error::stalled_channel peer reports zero progress error::slow_channel peer below statistical floor (mean − α·σ) network::error::service_stopped chaser is closed; update short-circuits error::success continue The peer-side reaction (drop connection vs. continue) lives in protocol_performer (doc 06 §4).

A formal model can represent chaser_download as a process with: inputs: bus messages (chase::* listed in §4) request RPCs: update, get_hashes, put_hashes (each carries a result_handler continuation) the compact timer tick outputs: bus messages (chase::download, chase::windowed, chase::purge, chase::split, chase::stall) returned codes to request RPCs state: position, requested, advanced ∈ ℕ inventory ∈ ℕ (latched after first nonzero) purging ∈ {true, false} -- abstracts job_ deferred, expired ∈ Link ∪ {⊥} maps : Queue of map -- each map is a non-empty set of (height, hash) pairs speeds : finite map from channel-id to ℝ⁺

No-overshoot: position ≤ requested and advanced ≤ requested are loop invariants. Purge soundness: while purging, maps = ∅ and no download is emitted. Bypass clamp (Download-Bypass-1): no requested height above the bypass height while the position is under it. Eventual progress: assuming peers honour get_hashes/put_hashes contracts, the position increases monotonically when not purging. Liveness; requires fairness on peer scheduling. Split correctness: chase::split(self) is sent only to notify_one(slow) where slow ≠ self (:228-247). Purge barrier completeness: every chase::purge is eventually followed by a chase::download (or by stop). This depends on the race_all semantics and peer compliance.

Peers eventually release job_ copies after chase::purge — the protocols layer guarantees this on stop (doc 06 §5.2). query.get_unassociated_above terminates and is monotone in requested_. The compact deferral is bounded by compact_timeout per top.

The three state machines (§3) are independent in their state space but interleaved in time — one actor per chaser with a single message-pump is sufficient. The race_all token (job_) is a non-trivial primitive. It is effectively a (condition-variable, ref-count) pair: each peer increments on get_hashes and decrements when done; the chaser waits on count → 0. set_unassociated is naturally a generator/iterator (lazy sequence of maps).

All do_* methods run on the strand. Race-freedom on internal state is by construction. The only externally-visible interaction beyond the bus is the peer speed/inventory protocol (§6, §7). Model the peer as a process that responds to slow_channel/exhausted_channel/stalled_channel return values by dropping or pausing its connection. A model of race_all requires a counted semaphore or refcount; this is the only place in chaser_download that needs more than single-threaded reasoning.

This is the authoritative, source-verified reference for every chase enumerator: payload, issuer sites, handler sites, and known discrepancies with the inline chase.hpp documentation. Every fact below is grep-derived against master at a5173475. Methodology and queries are in §4 so any future change can be re-verified mechanically.

event_subscriber_ : full_node // include/bitcoin/node/full_node.hpp:219 = network::desubscriber<object_key, event_value> // define.hpp:84 A desubscriber is the libbitcoin-network primitive that combines pub/sub with explicit unsubscription via a key. All subscribers share one bus.

event_value is a std::variant with one alternative per chase enumerator, declared in enum order in namespace chases (include/bitcoin/node/chase.hpp). Each payload struct carries a static constexpr chase id and zero or one field: Field Type Events — start, space, suspend, resume, unfull, stale, stop height height_t snap, bump, checked, windowed, valid, template_ branch_point height_t purge, headers, regressed, disorganized channel object_t starved, split, stall count / sequence count_t download / report link header_t unchecked, unvalid, confirmable, unconfirmable, block, pruned, organized, reorganized link transaction_t transaction A static_assert(is_chase_ordered(...)) guarantees the variant index equals the enumerator, so to_chase(value) is static_cast<chase>(value.index()) and to_payload<chase::X>(value) is a std::get by that index. Invariant (Bus-0). An event cannot carry the wrong payload type: the payload struct is the event. Handlers switch on to_chase(value) and read to_payload<chase::X>(value).field.

There are two subscribe APIs, both eventually owning state on the full_node strand: API Used by Strand discipline subscribe_chase(notifier) → object_key (sync) chasers, session_outbound Caller must already be on full_node strand subscribe_chase(notifier, completer) (async) protocols Posts to full_node strand internally; completer fires there Chaser subscription path (include/bitcoin/node/chasers/chaser.hpp:100-101, src/chasers/chaser.cpp:91-94): chaser::subscribe_chase → full_node::subscribe_chase(handler) // src/full_node.cpp:247-253 → event_subscriber_.subscribe(handler, key) Each chaser subscribes exactly once, in its start(), via SUBSCRIBE_CHASE(handle_chase, _1, _2) (chaser.hpp:166-167). The handle_chase body runs on the node strand and POSTs the work to the chaser's own strand. Protocol subscription path (src/protocols/protocol.cpp:183-232): protocol::subscribe_chase → session::subscribe_chase(handler, complete) // src/sessions/session.cpp:114-118 → full_node::subscribe_chase(handler, complete) // src/full_node.cpp:255-270 → posts to strand → do_subscribe_chase → event_subscriber_.subscribe(handler, key) → complete(ec, key) → protocol::handle_subscribe stores key_ → handle_subscribed posts subscribed() to channel strand The async variant exists because a protocol is constructed on its channel strand, not the node strand, so it must hop across. Subscription is asynchronous, so a protocol may miss events emitted before it completes (the source notes this at every protocol subscription site).

chaser/protocol calls notify(ec, chases::X{...}) → full_node::notify posts to strand // src/full_node.cpp:217-222 → do_notify on strand → event_subscriber_.notify(ec, value) // :225-229 → each subscriber's handle_chase runs here and POSTs to its own strand notify_one(key, ...) (:231-245) delivers to a single subscriber by key; it is used for chase::split (targeting the slowest channel) and for chase::stop on unsubscribe.

full_node::unsubscribe_chase(key) does not remove the entry; it sends a single chases::stop to that subscriber only (src/full_node.cpp:272-275). The subscriber's handle_chase returns false on chase::stop, and the desubscriber interprets that as removal. So: Invariant (Bus-1). A false return from handle_chase means "remove me". Every chaser returns false on chase::stop and when closed(); protocols return false when stopped(). Invariant (Bus-2). The bus is torn down only in full_node::do_close, which broadcasts chases::stop to all subscribers (src/full_node.cpp:154). After that point no further notify will deliver.

Notation: Issuer is every notify(... chases::X{...}) or notify_one(... chases::X{...}) call site that is not commented out. Direct self-calls of handle_chase (not through the bus) are listed as self. Handler is every case chase::X: arm that is not commented out. Discrepancies with the chase.hpp inline doc are flagged ⚠.

A formal model can treat the bus as follows. Processes. Each chaser and each event-subscribing protocol is a process P with: a single inbox typed (code, event_value) a private state space Σ_P a deterministic transition δ_P : Σ_P × (code, event_value) → Σ_P × Output_P where Output_P is a finite set of notify calls and outbound asynchronous actions (e.g. DB writes). Bus. The bus is broadcast-with-filter: every notify(ec, v) is delivered to every subscriber, and each subscriber's handle_chase inspects to_chase(v) to decide whether to act. notify_one is a point-to-point exception used only for split and stop. Invariants worth proving. Liveness of stop: after full_node::do_close, every process eventually reaches a terminal state. (Follows from Bus-2 + the universal case chase::stop: return false;.) Disorganize convergence: every chase::regressed/disorganized is eventually responded to by the consuming chasers' "rewind" branches (chaser_download.cpp:348-364, chaser_validate.cpp:170-177, chaser_confirm.cpp:129-132) before the next forward event is processed. No spurious validation: chase::valid is emitted only from chaser_validate::notify_block (chaser_validate.cpp:366), after either full validation, bypass processing, or batch verification of the height. Confirm uniqueness: chase::confirmable, unconfirmable, organized, reorganized, block, stale all have a single issuer (chaser_confirm). Confirmation is centralized. Two archivers: chase::checked and chase::unchecked have exactly two issuers — the download protocol and the compact block fill in chaser_transaction — and both write the block association before emitting (docs 06 §5.6, 11 §3). Dormant events (do not model as live). chase::snap — handler exists, no issuer. chase::template_ — handler is "miners" (external), no issuer in this repo. chase::report — issuer is the executor (external, libbitcoin-server). chase::confirmable — issued, no handler.

Companion to 06-sessions-and-protocols. protocol_filter_out_70015 is the light-client compact-block-filter serving protocol, implementing BIP157 (getcfcheckpt / getcfheaders / getcfilters) over the Neutrino filter type (BIP158). It handles three peer requests and replies with data derived from the filter records persisted by chaser_validate (set_filter_body) and chaser_confirm (set_filter_head). The protocol is stateless per channel — pure request/response. Filter bodies are streamed one message per block under the channel's gate. File Lines Role src/protocols/protocol_filter_out_70015.cpp 261 All three BIP157 request handlers

A client filter is a compact, deterministic summary of the scripts in a block (BIP158: Golomb-Rice encoded set of scriptPubKeys + spent prevout scripts). Light clients can ask any full node for these filters, scan them locally to find blocks relevant to their wallet, then fetch only those blocks. BIP157 is the P2P protocol for serving them: Filter checkpoint (getcfcheckpt): every 1000 blocks (the client_filter_checkpoint_interval), the filter header (a hash chain over filter bodies). Used by clients to anchor trust quickly. Filter headers (getcfheaders): a range of filter hashes from start_height to stop_hash inclusive, plus the filter header at start_height - 1. Up to max_client_filter_headers (2000) per request. Filters (getcfilters): the actual filter bodies for a range, up to max_client_filters (1000) per request. Only one filter type is recognised: client_filter::type_id::neutrino (BIP158). Anything else is a protocol violation. Invariant (Filter-Type-1). All three request handlers reject any filter_type != neutrino with protocol_violation. The node serves Neutrino filters or nothing.

All filter data is derived from already-persisted store records. The protocol performs no computation other than serialization; it can be modelled as a pure read transformer.

6. getcfilters handler and the streaming pattern

// :171-226 type, stop_hash, range checks as for cfheaders, with count ≤ max_client_filters (1000) const auto ancestry = std::make_shared<database::header_links>(); if (!query.get_ancestry(*ancestry, stop_link, count)) → protocol_violation span<milliseconds>(events::ancestry_msecs, start); send_filter(error::success, ancestry, gate()); return true; // :228-254 void send_filter(ec, ancestry, gate) { if (stopped(ec) || ancestry->empty()) return; const auto link = system::pop(*ancestry); if (!query.get_filter_body(out.filter, link)) { stop(protocol_violation); return; } out.block_hash = query.get_header_key(link); span<milliseconds>(events::filter_msecs, start); SEND(out, send_filter, _1, ancestry, gate); } This is a self-recursive async loop, identical in structure to protocol_block_out_106::send_block. The completion handler of each SEND is send_filter itself, with the same ancestry_ptr shared across iterations. The channel's gate is held across the loop so that another getcfilters arriving mid-stream cannot interleave with it; the handler stays subscribed (the earlier one-shot resubscribe trick is gone). Invariant (Filter-Stream-1). The ancestry list is consumed back-to-front (system::pop), so the wire order is start_height, start_height + 1, …, stop_height. This matches BIP157 expected ordering (low height first). Invariant (Filter-Stream-2). A failure to fetch any filter body mid-stream drops the peer (protocol_violation). The ancestry is abandoned when send_filter returns.

None. This protocol does not subscribe to or emit any chase events. Its sole inputs are peer messages; its sole outputs are peer messages and metrics events (events::filter_msecs, events::filterhashes_msecs, events::filterchecks_msecs, events::ancestry_msecs).

All errors result in dropping the peer; none are node-faults. Companion to 00-overview and 01-event-bus. chaser_header is the state machine that attaches headers to the candidate chain. It is the only organizer: blocks-first synchronization and the templated chaser_organize<Block> it shared with the header chaser were removed in September 2026, and the organizer was folded into this class. Headers reach it in three forms: proven headers from the header protocols (already validated and proven to a checkpoint or to a current top at minimum work, doc 07 §2), unproven headers announced by compact blocks, and prioritized headers re-evaluated from the tree as a manual tie break. File Role include/bitcoin/node/chasers/chaser_header.hpp Declaration, header_tree, strand-protected state src/chasers/chaser_header.cpp Implementation (925 lines)

The chaser does not own the chain — the database does. It manipulates two chain projections exposed by database::query: Projection Mutators called from organize Read methods used Candidate chain push_candidate(link), pop_candidate() get_top_candidate, to_top_candidate, to_candidate(height), is_candidate_header(link), get_candidate_fork(out fork_point), get_candidate_chain_state(settings, height) Confirmed chain — (organize never writes confirmed; see chaser_confirm) get_confirmed_fork(fork), get_confirmed_chain_state(settings, hash) Header records set_code(out link, header, ctx, work, milestone, compact), set_block_unconfirmable(link) to_header(hash), to_parent(link), is_unconfirmable(link), get_header(link), get_height(link), get_branch(out states, hash), get_work(out, states), get_strong_branch(out, work, branch_point, prioritized) Invariant (Organize-Store-1). Every store mutation in organize is performed on the chaser's own strand (src/chasers/chaser_header.cpp:195, :439 — both do_organize and do_disorganize open with BC_ASSERT(stranded())). Concurrent writes from other chasers do not occur in this class's scope; coordination across chasers happens via the event bus.

Initialised in start() (:76-78); updated at the end of every successful strong organize (:389); rewound by do_disorganize (:542-543). tree_ — a memory-resident map of weak-branch headers (headers whose branch does not beat the current candidate). Invariant (Organize-Mem-1). All of the above are set on the strand and read on the strand. bumped_ exists to suppress redundant validation bumps, not to enforce a chain property.

A checkpoint is a configured (hash, height) pair that fixes the chain. update_checkpoint(top) (:697-718) tracks the highest checkpoint reached by the candidate top (active_checkpoint_) and the next one above it; when a new checkpoint is reached, tree headers at or under it are purged (prune_tree(), :796-810). is_under_active_checkpoint(previous) (:671-695) refuses any header whose parent is stored below the active checkpoint — a fork under a reached checkpoint is a checkpoint_conflict before any state is computed. Extending the top, extending a tree header, and orphans are excluded from the test. Invariant (Organize-Checkpoint-1). Once the candidate reaches checkpoint C, no header forking below C is organized or cached. The set_reorganized assertion !is_under_checkpoint(height) (:588) follows: pops never descend under the top checkpoint. A milestone is a configured (hash, height) pair that does not fix the chain. It permits bypass of validation for blocks at or under it, if the milestone is on the archived branch. The milestone flag is decided by the header protocol while collecting a proven branch (milestone = height <= milestone_, doc 07 §2.3) and stored with the header by set_code (:755-756). This chaser does not track milestones itself.
Triggered by handle_chase on chase::unchecked, chase::unvalid, chase::unconfirmable when database.mark_unconfirmable is set (:142-189). Argument is the header_t link of the offending header.

After a successful run, post-conditions: set_block_unconfirmable has been called for the offending link and every candidate above it. The store now permanently marks these headers as bad (:489). The candidate chain top equals the previous confirmed chain top: every candidate above the fork point has been popped (:487-512); every confirmed block above the fork point has been re-pushed as candidate (:518-528). The valid portion of the candidate branch (below the bad link) has been re-cached into tree_ so that subsequent organize calls can re-promote it (:471-482). state_ is reset to the new (lower) candidate top (:542-543). chase::disorganized is published with payload = new fork point; downstream chasers (download, validate, confirm) rewind themselves to this height. chase::suspend is published; peer connections are dropped so that fresh connections resync headers. Invariant (Organize-Disorg-1). After chase::disorganized is emitted, the candidate top equals the confirmed top (modulo races; the confirmed interlock guarantees the snapshot used to compute the fork point is consistent, :452, :520). This is the strongest correctness obligation in the organize machine. Invariant (Organize-Disorg-2). chase::suspend follows chase::disorganized unconditionally on success (:546-549). The two emissions are not reordered. A specification can treat them as a single atomic publish.

Disorganize can be triggered while another disorganize is still in flight (a second chase::unvalid arrives). The is_candidate_header short-circuit at :446-447 handles this gracefully: the second call silently returns because the offending link is no longer on the candidate chain. There is no explicit lock. Invariant (Organize-Disorg-3). Repeated disorganize calls on the same link are idempotent: the second is a no-op after is_candidate_header(link) returns false.

tree_ is an in-memory cache of headers that have arrived but are not strong enough to archive. Two arrival paths: Weak branch (:293-299) — branch work doesn't beat the current candidate top (or ties it without prioritization). Disorganize (:471-482) — the valid portion of a rolled-back branch is re-cached with its chain state. Exit paths: push_header(key) (:647-657) — extracts from tree_, archives, pushes to candidate. do_prioritize (:400-427) — extracts a cached branch top for re-evaluation as prioritized. Pruning (below).

The tree is bounded by three prunes: Prune Trigger Rule prune_tree(threshold) :735-780 once per window of candidate progress (prune_tree(top), :783-794) erase every tree branch whose top has cumulative work under the window threshold, descending while each parent has no other child prune_tree() :797-810 a new checkpoint reached (update_checkpoint) erase every tree header at or under the active checkpoint shrink_tree(current) :723-732 first current organize (one-shot, shrunk_) rehash the map to release bucket capacity used during catch-up The window is currency_window_minutes × 60 / block_spacing_seconds blocks (get_window, :816-821), and the work threshold is the candidate top's cumulative work less one window of its proof (get_window_work, :824-831). A zero currency window disables the work prune. Invariant (Organize-Tree-1). A tree branch survives a window prune only if its top's cumulative work is at least the candidate top's work less one window of proof. A peer cannot hold memory with a dead branch for longer than one window of candidate progress. Invariant (Organize-Tree-2). Every tree header carries its chain state (cache sets it, :659-666), so get_chain_state can extend a tree branch without touching the store (:833-850).

do_get_minimum_work (:430-435) answers the header protocols with max(settings.minimum_work, get_window_work()): a proven branch must reach at least the candidate top's work less one window, so a peer cannot make the node archive a branch that is far behind.

A manual tie break between equal-work branches, bitcoind's preciousblock analogue (:398-427). The hash must be the top of a cached branch; it is extracted and reorganized with prioritized = true, which get_strong_branch treats as "at least equal work". The preference is not retained: the reorganized branch then wins ties.

Every numbered fault is a terminal (calls chaser::fault which suspends the network and is meant to indicate a programmer or store-corruption error). For a formal model, each is a proof obligation: "this branch is unreachable under the system invariants". 8. Differences from the inline chase.hpp comments

(For book-keeping; cross-reference with 01-event-bus §2.) chase::bump "issued by 'organize'": this chaser (:378) plus chaser_validate on silent drain. chase::headers "issued by 'header'". ✓ (:384). chase::regressed / disorganized "issued by 'organize'". ✓ (:326, :546). chase::suspend "issued by 'full_node'": incomplete, this chaser also emits it after a disorganize (:549). chase::unchecked / unvalid / unconfirmable "handled by 'organize'": ✓, with the mark_unconfirmable gate.

The state machine is naturally functional. do_organize reads as a pipeline of Maybe-returning steps with the store as an effectful argument: the DB writes and bus emits are the only effectful boundaries; everything between them is pure computation over (header, parent_state, settings). tree_ is a hash table keyed by header hash. The old unbounded-tree concern is addressed by the window and checkpoint prunes (§6.2); an LRU cap would open a vector where an attacker evicts legitimate weak branches, which the work threshold does not. get_branch_work walks tree_ by parent-hash chain into the store (:854-890) — straightforward recursion that also yields the ordered branch for the reorg.

The whole state machine is strand-confined, so single-threaded semantics suffice for proving local invariants. The store is treated as an oracle: every numbered failure mode organizeN reduces to a store-consistency assumption. Strongest provable property: after every do_organize that returns success, the candidate top has either (a) advanced strictly forward, (b) reorganized to a different top with at least as much work, or (c) the header is cached in tree_. Cases (a)/(b) coincide with emission of chase::headers when current; (c) does not emit. The "after disorganize, candidate == confirmed" post-condition (Organize-Disorg-1) is the hinge for downstream chasers: download, validate, confirm all use it to bound their rewind. A useful proof structure: define Φ(σ) = "candidate chain in σ has cumulative work W and parent of top has W − proof(top)" as a loop invariant for the reorg phase (F) — every iteration of the inner loops at :331-350 preserves it.

Companion to 06-sessions-and-protocols and 02-chaser-header. The header protocols are the wire-side of chaser_header: they sync headers from peers (protocol_header_in_*) and serve headers to peers (protocol_header_out_*). There are three versioned levels: 31800: classic. Sync via get_headers/headers; announcements discovered indirectly via inv messages. 70012 (BIP130): adds sendheaders — peers announce new blocks directly with headers messages, bypassing inv. 70014 (BIP152 version 2): adds compact block announcement and fill. Attached when network.enable_compact and the peer negotiated bip152. Each level inherits from the one below in both directions — an extension, not a replacement. Header sync is prove-then-archive: a peer's branch is validated and discarded header by header while sampling hashes, until it is proven (reaches a checkpoint, or is exhausted while current and at the minimum work); only then is it requested again and organized as proven against the samples. The node never archives a branch it has not seen through to proof, which closes the weak-headers DoS surface. // :44-54, :57-87 void start() { SUBSCRIBE_CHANNEL(headers, ...); get_minimum_work(BIND(handle_minimum_work, _1, _2, true)); ... } void do_minimum_work(ec, work, initial) { minimum_work_ = work; if (initial) SEND(create_get_headers()); } Sync begins once the minimum work is first obtained from the header chaser (doc 02 §6.3) and is refreshed on every restart (:294-295). The initial locator is built from the archived candidate chain (create_get_headers(), :439-447).

Synchronize (:121-202). Each header must connect to state_ (else orphan_header); it is validated with chaser_header::validate (header check, accept, checkpoint conflict) and its chain state rolled forward, then discarded. Every interval_ heights the hash is sampled; a milestone match records milestone_; a checkpoint height proves the branch immediately. A message that does not extend the branch restarts from the parent of its first header if that parent is stored (restart, :281-297): a single unknown-parent header is an announcement from a peer that is ahead, so headers are requested from the top candidate; multiple unknown-parent headers mean the peer does not connect to the locator and it is dropped (:138-154). Prove (:327-341). Records top_, adds the top hash as the last sample if not on an interval, switches to archiving_ and requests the branch again from its parent. Collect (:205-278). Headers are buffered until the next sample height (each interval and the top). The hash at that height must equal the next sample (else unexpected_header); the buffered segment is then organized as proven, with milestone = height <= milestone_ per header. Reaching top_ resumes synchronization above it with state_ retained; exhaustion before top_ means the peer no longer presents the branch, so it is discarded. Finish (:344-358). The peer is exhausted. The branch is proven if it extends the start height, its top is current, and its cumulative work is at least minimum_work_; otherwise sync completes without archiving anything. Sample budget (:300-324). The sample vector is bounded by database.header.expected / 2000 (default 1024): at the budget every other sample is dropped and interval_ doubles, retaining the samples at multiples of the new interval. Invariant (HeaderIn-Prove-1). A header is organized only as part of a branch that was validated end to end from a stored parent to a proof point, and only after each collected segment matched a hash sampled during that validation. Memory per channel is bounded by the sample budget plus one interval of buffered headers. Invariant (HeaderIn-Prove-2). A proof point is a checkpoint, or a current top at or above the minimum work. The minimum work is at least the candidate top's work less one currency window (doc 02 §6.3), so a peer cannot cause archival of a branch that is far behind the candidate. Invariant (HeaderIn-Sync-1). Each channel syncs independently from the candidate top. With many parallel channels, each will converge to the same head — duplicates are dropped by chaser_header::do_organize (returns error::duplicate_header, ignored by handle_organize, :361-390).

Invariant (HeaderIn-Subscribe-1). Announcement subscription is gated on is_current_chain(true) — confirmed chain is current. Until then, the protocol does only initial sync. Invariant (HeaderIn-Subscribe-2). subscribed is one-shot: latched true on first successful complete(), never reset.
Inside handle_receive_headers (:105-107): once subscribed, every received header hash is recorded as "announced-from-this-peer", to be checked by the out protocols so we don't echo them back (§8).

47 lines. Only override: complete() (:31-44): if not yet subscribed, latch and SEND(send_headers{}) (BIP130), then call the base. Because subscribed is set first, the base skips the inv subscription. Announcements then arrive as headers messages and flow through handle_receive_headers exactly like sync: a single header with an unknown parent is treated as an announcement from a peer that is ahead (§2.3).

Fill a current block announced as a compact block from the transaction pool instead of downloading it. The protocol subscribes to sendcmpct, cmpctblock and blocktxn (:41-54) and requests high-bandwidth compact blocks from the peer once the chain is current, whichever of the peer's sendcmpct signal and currency comes last (upgrade, :80-93).

Source: handle_receive_compact_block :98-133, collect :181-227, decode :231-266, scan :269-303, request :306-323, handle_receive_compact_transactions :328-382, identify :387-434, handle_submit_compact :489-525. Invariant (Compact-Fill-1). A compact block is filled only when it extends a current candidate (is_candidate_extension) and at most compact_missing_percent of its txs are missing from the pool; otherwise the block is left to normal download, which chaser_download defers by compact_timeout to give the fill a chance (doc 03 §7). Invariant (Compact-Fill-2). One fill at a time per channel (fill_), and a blocktxn is accepted only for the block in fill_ with exactly the requested count; each received tx must hash to the short id at its position (the coinbase short id is over its witness serialization), else the peer is dropped. Invariant (Compact-Fill-3). The block is identified (merkle root over txids with 64-byte malleation check, witness commitment over wtxids) before submission. The transaction chaser then validates and archives the unpooled txs in block order and associates the block, emitting chase::checked (doc 11 §3).

An unidentified compact block cannot be attributed to the peer until the block is archived by another path. The protocol holds evidence (link, witness root, tx count, :417-419) and resolves it on the peer's next compact block: if the evidence block is now associated and does not match the archived witness commitment and count, the peer sent an invalid compact block and is dropped; a resend of the block in evidence is not filled while it remains unarchived (resolve, :533-566).

Subscribes to sendcmpct (:39-48). A version-2 high-bandwidth sendcmpct from the peer activates the announcement subscription (:83-97). do_announce (:53-78) then sends a compact block built by make_compact_block (coinbase prefilled, short ids over wtxids) when the peer wants compact blocks and did not announce the block to us; otherwise it falls back to the 70012 headers announcement when the peer also sent sendheaders. The 70012 block-out inv path is superseded in both cases (doc 08 §4).

Lives on node::channel_peer (src/channels/channel_peer.cpp:32-42). Each channel keeps the hashes announced to it in a rolling bloom filter (node::rolling_bloom_filter, src/rolling_bloom_filter.cpp): Three generations of max_inventory (50,000) hashes each. When the current generation is full, the oldest is cleared and becomes current, so the filter retains at least the most recent 100,000 hashes. Each generation is a bloom array of 20 probes over 1,442,696 bits (about 176 KiB, allocated on its first insert), keyed by the first 8 bytes of the hash. The false positive rate is about 2^-20 per generation, at most about 3 in 2^20 for the three together. There is no setting; every channel has the filter. set_announced(hash): called by header-in (headers after subscription, compact blocks) and tx-in (every announced tx) when receiving an announcement. was_announced(hash): called by header-out, block-out and tx-out before sending an announcement. This is not global state; it's per-channel — exactly what's needed to break the local A↔B echo. Invariant (Anti-Echo-1). The pair (set_announced, was_announced) guarantees a peer that announced X to us is never sent X back, on that channel, while X is within the last 100,000 announcements. A false positive may withhold an announcement the peer has not seen. It does not guarantee global no-duplication.

No archival without proof (HeaderIn-Prove-1, HeaderIn-Prove-2). No echo within a channel (Anti-Echo-1). Sync convergence: assuming a peer's header chain extends ours and is proven, each get_headers reply strictly extends the candidate chain (or is empty). Convergence after 2⌈Δ/2000⌉ round-trips where Δ is the gap (one pass to prove, one to archive). Compact identity before submission (Compact-Fill-3).
Each channel makes progress as long as the peer responds to get_headers. After complete(), the channel quiesces until the peer sends a headers, cmpctblock (70014) or inv (31800) message.

The sync is two passes over the branch; the second is the one that writes. The sample vector is the only memory held across them. BIP130 and BIP152 are strict extensions over 31800; mirror that with a class hierarchy or trait composition. set_announced/was_announced is a per-channel bounded FIFO.

The in protocol is stateful in the sync bookkeeping (§11.1); the proof points (checkpoint, current-and-minimum-work) are the obligations that tie it to chaser_header. The compact fill is a per-channel single-slot state machine whose correctness obligations are identity-before-submit and short-id verification; the pool side is in doc 11. The end-to-end "candidate chain converges to peer's tip" property requires reasoning across multiple channels — out of scope of a per-protocol spec but provable given chaser_header's safety properties.

Source-anchored architecture documentation for libbitcoin-node: the chasers, the event bus, sessions and peer protocols. This is a top-down, source-anchored description of libbitcoin-node. It is also written to support a formal-verification effort, which needs state machines, invariants, pre/post-conditions, and a clear bus-vs.-store ownership model. The architectural concepts (parallel block download, sequential chasers following concurrent download and validation, validation bypass by checkpoints and milestones, append-only store writes with small copyable indexes, and quiescence for snapshot, remap and shutdown) are from the 2021 design document for the version 4 node. Every behavioural claim is anchored with file:line references into the C++ source so it can be re-verified or re-derived if source drifts. The citations in this revision were verified against libbitcoin-node master at commit a5173475 (2026-10-20), with chaser_check renamed to chaser_download (node branch download, ea1e1264).

Purpose. This document is the top-down map of the node and the entry point for the deeper subsystem docs. It also serves a formal-verification effort, which needs explicit state machines, invariants, and concurrency boundaries. All non-trivial claims are anchored with path/to/file.ext:line citations into the C++ so they can be re-derived if the source drifts. Citations are against libbitcoin-node master at a5173475.

libbitcoin is a stack of cooperating libraries. The node sits at the top and composes the lower layers; it adds no new I/O primitives — only the chain state machine, the transaction pool, and the orchestration of validation across many threads. The node owns no executable. Embedders construct one full_node (include/bitcoin/node/full_node.hpp:32) against an externally-owned query& (the database handle) and a configuration&, then call start() → run() → close().

Key facts: full_node is a network::net subclass (include/bitcoin/node/full_node.hpp:32-33). Networking (peer discovery, channels, message framing) is inherited unchanged from libbitcoin-network. The node only adds chasers and overrides session attachment to use node-specific sessions. full_node owns the nine chasers as direct members (include/bitcoin/node/full_node.hpp:210-218). They are constructed in order at full_node construction (src/full_node.cpp:44-52) and live exactly as long as the node. All chasers share a single event_subscriber_ (include/bitcoin/node/full_node.hpp:219) — this is the central event bus. The store is not owned by full_node; only a reference to a query is held (src/full_node.cpp:43). Lifetime is the embedder's responsibility. full_node is a pure forwarder for the chaser entry points: organize variants and prioritize/get_minimum_work go to chaser_header_ (src/full_node.cpp:161-188), submit/submit_compact to chaser_transaction_ (:190-201), get_hashes/put_hashes and performance to chaser_download_ (:203-212, :486-490), and estimate to chaser_estimate_ (:480-484).

Context Scope Where defined full_node strand Event-bus mutation; chaser start inherited from network::net Per-chaser strand One strand per chaser, on the network pool src/chasers/chaser.cpp:35 (strand_(node.service()...)) Validation threadpool chaser_validate only: own pool + own strand src/chasers/chaser_validate.cpp:39-41, :393-401 Scan threadpool chaser_transaction only: one thread src/chasers/chaser_transaction.cpp:39 Per-channel strand One strand per peer channel/protocol inherited from network::channel Invariant (Concurrency-1). Every chaser method that mutates chaser state must be on that chaser's own strand. The base provides strand(), stranded(), and the BIND/POST templates to enforce this (include/bitcoin/node/chasers/chaser.hpp:58-70, :110-117). Invariant (Concurrency-2). All event_subscriber_ mutation (subscribe, notify, notify_one, stop) happens on the full_node strand (src/full_node.cpp:217-270). Calls from chasers/protocols are posted into that strand by full_node::notify / notify_one (:217-222, :231-237).

Implementation: full_node::notify posts to strand(), then do_notify calls event_subscriber_.notify(...) (src/full_node.cpp:217-229). Each subscriber's handle_chase runs on the node strand and immediately POSTs the real work to its own strand, so chaser state is only touched stranded. Invariant (Concurrency-3). A chaser subscription is created via subscribe_chase from the chaser's start() (include/bitcoin/node/chasers/chaser.hpp:100-101), which runs on the node strand (src/full_node.cpp:75-95). Protocols subscribe via the async variant (include/bitcoin/node/full_node.hpp:111-113) which posts to the strand and uses a completer.

Chasers do consensus-critical, often expensive work (script execution, database writes, snapshotting). Each strand allows the chaser to serialize its own mutations while still running in parallel with the other chasers (include/bitcoin/node/chasers/chaser.hpp:30-35). This is one of the two main axes of parallelism in the node. The chasers form a pipeline; each stage runs on its own strand and they communicate by publishing events. The other axis, equally important, is per-channel strands: every peer connection also runs on its own strand. Peers and chasers therefore execute concurrently with each other, bounded only by the shared threadpool size. chaser_validate additionally fans block validation out over its own pool (doc 04).

The node, with the network and system layers beneath it and the server above it, is lock-free: at every point some thread completes its step, whatever the scheduling of the others, because no thread ever waits on another. Strands order work, they do not block threads. Posting to a busy strand queues the handler and returns. The posting thread continues with other work; a strand serializes handlers, not threads. Cross-thread state is atomic. State shared outside a strand is std::atomic: latches and counters such as chaser_validate's validate_backlog_ and bank flags (doc 04), chaser_snapshot::pruned_ (doc 12), protocol_block_out_70012::superseded_ (doc 08), and the network's suspend flags and channel counts (network/net.hpp:381-388). Results cross strands by posting. A broadcast that gathers a result from many channels (diagnostics) has each channel post its row to the collector's strand, and the collector reads them after the round completes (network broadcast/diagnostics.hpp, server protocol_bitcoind::to_collector, branch lockfree). System code waits on no other thread. A parallel algorithm (std::for_each under execution::par) fans a loop out over the pool and joins it, which is the caller's own work. Batch signature capture registers each thread's rows once, on first use, as a static initializer does (chain/signatures.cpp). GPU verification queues callers for the device (crypto/secp256k1/cuda/turns.hpp), which is arbitration of hardware, not of shared state. Invariant (Concurrency-4). No node, network, server or system code waits on another thread for shared state. State is owned by one strand, handed between strands by post, or held in an atomic. Store locking (database 04 §8) is internal to the database and hidden from the network stack.

The bus carries a code (error) and an event_value, which is a std::variant of one payload struct per chase enumerator (include/bitcoin/node/chase.hpp). The variant alternative index is the chase value (static_assert(is_chase_ordered(...))), so an event carries its own type: to_chase(value) recovers the enumerator and to_payload<chase::X>(value) the typed payload. Payload fields are height, branch_point, link (header_t or transaction_t), channel (object_t), count or sequence (count_t), or nothing. The enum is the specification of inter-chaser coupling. There is also a parallel, lower-volume events enum (include/bitcoin/node/events.hpp:28-71) — these are reporting events (metrics: archived/validated/confirmed/organized counts, batch and filter timespans), surfaced via reporter::fire and network::net::span<...>. The nine chasers form a directed pipeline. The diagram below is a conceptual sketch; the authoritative, source-verified issuer/handler graph is in 01-event-bus §3. Synchronization is headers-first only. Headers are synced by the header protocols, which validate and prove each peer's branch before archiving it (doc 07); the header chaser organizes proven headers into the candidate chain (doc 02); chaser_download partitions unassociated candidates into download windows (doc 03); blocks are identified and archived by protocol_block_in_31800 (doc 06) or filled from the pool by compact blocks (docs 07, 11); chaser_validate validates (doc 04) and chaser_confirm confirms (doc 05). The blocks-first mode and its chaser_block organizer were removed in September 2026.

Citations: src/full_node.cpp:63-73 (start), src/full_node.cpp:75-95 (do_start), src/full_node.cpp:97-119 (run / do_run), src/full_node.cpp:121-156 (close / do_close). Invariant (Lifecycle-1). The store must be initialised before start: full_node::start short-circuits with error::store_uninitialized if query_.is_initialized() is false (src/full_node.cpp:65-69). Invariant (Lifecycle-2). do_close initiates non-blocking stopping(...) on every chaser first, then event_subscriber_.stop(...), then net::do_close; close() then blocks on per-chaser stop(), which joins the validation and scan threadpools. Order matters: chasers must observe stop before the bus is torn down (src/full_node.cpp:121-156). Invariant (Lifecycle-3). chaser_snapshot::start may prune the store before the network starts, when the confirmed top is above genesis and the store is coalesced (src/chasers/chaser_snapshot.cpp:68-92). This is the only chaser whose start() performs a store write.

suspend(ec) calls net::suspend and emits chases::suspend with error::suspended_channel (src/full_node.cpp:301-306). resume() refuses when the store is full or faulted, otherwise calls net::resume and then emits chases::resume (:280-298). fault(ec) is the unified "something terminal happened" entry; it dispatches by store state — is_full → chases::space; is_fault → log the unrecoverable store fault; otherwise log a resumable node fault — and always calls suspend(ec) (:308-330). prune / snapshot / reload (:333-397) share a pattern: suspend the network, run the store operation, leave the network suspended (caller resumes on success). Each emits a metrics event (events::prune_msecs, events::snapshot_secs, events::reload_msecs). reload returns immediately when the store is not full (:377-378). Invariant (Store-1). During a store maintenance operation, all peer connections are suspended; the caller is responsible for resume() after success. A wait_lock event during the op causes a renewed suspend (src/full_node.cpp:343-344, :364-365, :389-390) — racy connections that missed the first suspend are caught here.

Four predicates on full_node gate most behaviour (src/full_node.cpp:432-470): Predicate Meaning is_current_time(ts) ts is within node.currency_window_minutes of now; a zero window is always current is_current_chain(confirmed) the candidate (false) or confirmed (true) top timestamp is current is_current_header(link) the header's stored timestamp is current is_recent() confirmed top reached node.maximum_height, or the confirmed chain is current "Recent" is weaker than "current": a node deliberately limited to a fixed height can activate inbound service and block serving at that ceiling.

full_node overrides three session-attachment hooks (src/full_node.cpp:495-508): attach_manual_session → node::session_manual attach_inbound_session → node::session_inbound attach_outbound_session → node::session_outbound Each node::session_* adds a node::session mixin (include/bitcoin/node/sessions/session.hpp) which forwards to full_node (organize, submit, get/put_hashes, notify, subscribe, estimate, performance). The mixin's job is to give every protocol instance on every channel a reference to the node's event bus and organizers. session_outbound additionally subscribes to the bus to reduce outbound connections while recent (doc 06 §1.4). Protocols are versioned by Bitcoin P2P protocol number: Family Versions Direction header 31800, 70012 (BIP130), 70014 (BIP152) in header 31800, 70012, 70014 out block 31800 in block 106, 70001 (BIP37 not_found), 70012, 70014 out tx 106, 70001, 70013 (BIP133), 70016 (BIP339) in tx 106, 60002 (BIP35), 70001, 70013, 70016 out filter 70015 (BIP157/158) out meta observer, peer, performer — Each protocol class lives in include/bitcoin/node/protocols/ and is implemented in src/protocols/. protocol_block_in_31800 is the central performance-sensitive class — it's the only protocol referenced from many chase event handlers (download, starved, split, stall, purge, report, checked, unchecked). See 06 §5.

block_arena / block_memory (include/bitcoin/node/block_arena.hpp, block_memory.hpp, src/block_arena.cpp) implement an arena allocator for block-shaped objects. In the current source the arena is not wired into channel construction: session_peer::create_channel passes no memory controller (include/bitcoin/node/impl/sessions/session_peer.ipp:42-52) and full_node holds no block_memory member. Blocks received by protocol_block_in_31800 are chain::view::block instances over the wire buffer, identified and written to the store without materializing the full block object (src/protocols/protocol_block_in_31800.cpp:263-365). Implementation note. A formal model can abstract block contents as immutable values; the allocator is below the spec layer.

01 — Event bus: every chase event with its verified issuer and handler sites. 02 — Header chaser: header organization, tree pruning and disorganization. 03 — Download chaser: block download orchestration and the download window. 04 — Validation chaser: consensus validation and batched verification. 05 — Confirmation chaser: order-based consensus checks and the confirmed chain. 06 — Sessions and protocols: sessions, the protocol attach tree and protocol_block_in_31800. 07 — Header protocols: header sync and compact blocks. 08 — Block out protocols: serving blocks to peers. 09 — Filter out protocol: BIP157/158 client filters. 10 — Transaction protocols: transaction relay in and out. 11 — Transaction chaser: the transaction pool and compact block fill. 12 — Periphery chasers: snapshot, storage, template and fee estimate.

Chaser: a long-running strand-confined state machine that owns one responsibility in the blockchain pipeline (header organization, validation, the transaction pool, etc.). Organize: the act of attaching a header to the candidate chain. Candidate chain: the chain of headers the node prefers but has not yet fully confirmed. Confirmed chain: the chain of blocks that have passed all consensus checks and been committed. Proven header: a header whose branch the header protocol has validated end to end to a checkpoint or to a current top at minimum work; organized without re-validation. Milestone / checkpoint: configured (hash, height) pairs. A checkpoint fixes the chain; a milestone only permits validation bypass of blocks at or under it when it is on the candidate branch. Bypass: a block under the top checkpoint or the active milestone; identified and archived but not script-validated. Strand: a network::io::strand, which serializes execution of posted callbacks; the node uses one per chaser and one per channel. Event bus: event_subscriber_ on full_node; carries typed chases::* payloads between chasers and protocols. Window: the download window of chaser_download (maximum_concurrency blocks above the position); chase::windowed marks its completion. Bank: one of two store-side batch tables (signatures, silent payments); commits fill one bank while the other drains.

Companion to the core-pipeline chaser docs 02–05 and 11. The four chasers covered here are operationally peripheral to consensus. Chaser Role Current state Bus events chaser_snapshot Startup prune, one-shot prune on first current block, explicit snapshot Live (snapshot trigger dormant) Consumes block, snap; emits pruned chaser_storage Disk-space recovery + reload after full Fully live Consumes space; emits unfull chaser_template Mining template construction Stub Consumes transaction chaser_estimate Fee estimation accumulator Live when fee_estimate_horizon is nonzero Consumes pruned, block, organized, reorganized, transaction File Lines src/chasers/chaser_snapshot.cpp 315 src/chasers/chaser_storage.cpp 189 src/chasers/chaser_template.cpp 93 src/chasers/chaser_estimate.cpp 275 include/bitcoin/node/estimator.hpp 190 All four inherit from the base chaser, run on their own strand on the network pool, and subscribe to the bus in start().

Three triggers: Startup prune: in start(), before the network starts, when the confirmed top is above genesis and the store is coalesced, prune the prevout cache and emit chases::pruned{ top } (chaser_snapshot.cpp:68-92). One-shot prune on announce: when the confirmed chain first announces a current block (chase::block), prune once if coalesced; latched by pruned_ (:141-148, :166-202). Explicit snapshot: on chase::snap(height), take a full store snapshot. No issuer of chase::snap exists in this repo — dormant (doc 01 §2.1).

// chaser_snapshot.hpp:43 std::atomic_bool pruned_{}; // one-shot latch for prune The periodic-snapshot thresholds (snapshot_bytes/valid/confirm) remain commented out in source and settings. Invariant (Snapshot-State-1). pruned_ is set at most once per process lifetime, either by the startup prune or by the first successful announce-time prune. After it is set, chase::block events are dropped at the handler (:143-144).

// :141-153 case chase::block: if (!pruned_) POST(do_prune, link); case chase::snap: POST(do_snap, height); do_prune(link) — :166-202 Returns silently if already pruned, closed, or not coalesced. Calls the base chaser::prune (a wrapper around full_node::prune, doc 00 §6.2), which suspends the network, runs query.prune, and leaves the network suspended. On success: latch pruned_, emit chases::pruned{ link }, and resume() if the chaser was running before and the store is not full. On failure (typically not coalesced following a suspend) the prune is retried on the next announce. Invariant (Snapshot-Prune-1). pruned_ is latched and chase::pruned emitted before resume(), because the resumption is observable (the fee estimator initializes on pruned, and organization resumes with it). Invariant (Snapshot-Prune-2). Prune is gated on archive().is_coalesced(). If the store isn't ready, the handler returns silently; the next chase::block re-triggers it. do_snap(height) — :204-212 Calls take_snapshot(height) (:229-288), which calls the base chaser::snapshot(handler): same suspend/resume dance as prune. Currently unreachable — no chase::snap issuer in source.

When the node faults with a full disk (chase::space), monitor free space on the store volume and reload + resume once space becomes available. It owns a one-second network::deadline on its own strand (chaser_storage.cpp:51).
// :48-55 start: create timer; subscribe // :57-71 stopping: stop and reset the timer on the strand // :76-99 handle_chase: chase::space → POST(do_space); stop → false

// :116-141 handle_timer if (archive().is_fault() || !to_bool(archive().get_space())) return; // monitor the space condition, not suspension if (!have_capacity()) { disk_timer_->start(...); return; } do_reload(); // :143-174 do_reload ec = reload(...); if (ec == database::error::reload_locked) { disk_timer_->start(...); return; } // in-flight accessors: wait if (ec) { LOGF(...); return; } notify(error::success, chases::unfull{}); // before resume, so validate latches recovery resume(); Invariant (Storage-Loop-1). The polling loop exits exactly when: the store is faulted, the space condition has cleared (get_space() is zero), or a reload succeeded. Suspension state is not consulted, because other suspensions start and stop independently. Invariant (Storage-Reload-1). archive().reload(handler) is called only after file::space reports at least get_space() bytes free. A locked reload (accessors still holding the map) is a wait, not a failure; any other reload error ends monitoring. Invariant (Storage-Unfull-1). chase::unfull precedes chase::resume (emitted inside resume()), so chaser_validate can latch recovery before the suspension gate lifts and reset its position once its backlog clears (doc 04 §6.2).

Stub for mining-template construction (chaser_template.cpp). Subscribes to chase::transaction and posts an empty do_transaction (:53-88). The TODOs note the intended behaviour: recompute the block template on chain top change and on transaction graph change, and emit chase::template_(height) to wake an external miner. chase::template_ has no live issuer. A spec can treat this chaser as identity until it is implemented.

Maintains a running fee estimate over the confirmed chain and the pool, answering full_node::estimate(target, mode) (exposed to the server's RPC surface). Enabled when node.fee_estimate_horizon is nonzero (fee_estimate_enabled()); otherwise estimate returns estimate_disabled without subscribing (chaser_estimate.cpp:45-53, :64-74).

// chaser_estimate.hpp:67-73 std::atomic_bool stopping_{}; // cancels initialization std::atomic_bool initialized_{}; // estimator ready (thread safe) estimator::ptr estimator_{}; // heap allocated (large accumulator), strand-only bool pruned_{}; // initialization waits for the prune

Event When not initialized When initialized chase::pruned do_pruned: set pruned_, try do_initialize ignored chase::block do_initialize (retry each current block) ignored chase::organized ignored do_organized: push the block's fee rates (skipping backlogged heights at or under the accumulator top) chase::reorganized ignored do_reorganized: pop the block's rates (skipping heights above the top) chase::transaction ignored do_transaction: pool the tx's rate do_initialize (:192-214) requires the prune (which rewrites the pool) and a chain at least horizon blocks long, then builds the estimator from the last horizon confirmed blocks and the pooled transactions (estimator::initialize, cancellable by stopping_). Invariant (Estimate-Init-1). The accumulator is initialized once, after the first prune and only when the confirmed chain reaches the horizon; organization events that arrive during initialization are reconciled by height against the accumulator top (:231-233, :255-257). Invariant (Estimate-Consistency-1). Only txs that were pooled before confirmation contribute (by blocks waited from pool entry to confirmation); a conflict unpends the displaced txs. Push and pop are exact inverses on the decayed buckets, so a reorganization leaves the accumulator as if the popped block had never been organized.

include/bitcoin/node/estimator.hpp defines modes (basic, geometric, economical, conservative), three horizons (12, 48 and 1008 blocks), 283 geometric fee-rate bins from 0.1 to 100,000 sat/vB with step 1.05, decay-weighted per-bucket confirmation counters, and pending/aged slots for unconfirmed pooled txs. estimate(target, mode) returns satoshis per virtual byte, or estimate_failed (max_uint64), which the chaser maps to error::estimate_false; a call before initialization returns estimate_premature. The algorithm itself is out of scope here.

These four chasers contribute little to the global proof obligation set; the one obligation that touches the pipeline is Storage-Unfull-1 (ordering of unfull before resume). chaser_snapshot's pruned_ latch is a standard monotone Boolean; Snapshot-Prune-1 orders the latch and pruned before the resumption. chaser_storage's polling loop is a classic "wait until precondition holds" pattern; formally a liveness property "if chase::space is emitted and disk eventually has capacity, the system eventually resumes". chaser_estimate is a pure function of the event stream once initialized; Estimate-Consistency-1 (push/pop inverse) is the property worth stating.

Companion to 00-overview, 01-event-bus, and the chaser docs 02–05. This doc covers: Session layer — how full_node wires the node's chasers into libbitcoin-network's session machinery via a thin mixin, and the decision tree that determines which P2P protocols attach to a new channel. protocol_block_in_31800 — the heaviest peer-side class. It is the counterpart of chaser_download on the wire side: pulls download maps from chaser_download, sends getdata, receives blocks, identifies and archives them, and emits chase::checked per block. The supporting bases protocol, protocol_peer, protocol_observer, protocol_performer are described where they matter.
