libbitcoin-node deliberately avoids diamond inheritance: node::session is a sibling, not a parent, of network::session. The same applies to protocols.

session_peer<NetworkSession> is a class template whose NetworkSession parameter is instantiated separately for each concrete session: network::session_outbound, network::session_inbound, and network::session_manual (include/bitcoin/node/sessions/session_peer.hpp:33-62). The template inherits from its parameter (the network base) and also from node::session (the mixin). The node::session mixin (src/sessions/session.cpp:34-240) is pure forwarding: every method delegates to the held full_node&. So at the session layer, there is no node-specific state; the mixin's only role is to give protocols a typed handle on the node.

services_provided() ORs the node's configured service bits (provide_blocks, provide_witness, provide_filters, provide_privacy) into the network's (session_peer.ipp:28-33). relay() requests tx relay in the version handshake only when the confirmed chain is current (:35-39). create_channel constructs a node::channel_peer (:41-52). attach_handshake sets the channel's start height from the confirmed top before the version exchange (:54-68). attach_protocols is the attach tree (§2.3).

// src/sessions/session_inbound.cpp:26-29 bool session_inbound::enabled() const NOEXCEPT { return !node_settings().delay_inbound || is_recent(); } Invariant (Session-Inbound-1). Inbound connection attempts are rejected (the network layer disables the listener) until either delay_inbound == false or the confirmed chain is "recent" (full_node::is_recent: top equals configured maximum height or the confirmed top timestamp is within the currency window, doc 00 §6.3). This prevents a not-yet-caught-up node from serving stale data while still allowing bounded-height test deployments. This is implemented via enabled() rather than the bus suspend/resume mechanism so that the listener has independent control flow.

session_outbound (src/sessions/session_outbound.cpp:37-100) requires the configured node services of its peers (services_required), and subscribes to the bus after start when node.current_connections is nonzero. On chase::block and chase::stale it calls update_connections, which sets the outbound target to current_connections while is_recent() and to the configured network.outbound.connections otherwise. Invariant (Session-Outbound-1). While the confirmed chain is recent and current_connections is nonzero, the outbound session maintains at most current_connections peers; the full configured count is restored when the chain goes stale.

Returns a node::channel_peer upcast to network::channel. The node channel adds the per-channel anti-echo filter (a rolling bloom filter of announced hashes, src/channels/channel_peer.cpp:32-42) and stamps the witness parse context on every inbound frame (include/bitcoin/node/channels/channel_peer.hpp:54-61), so messages are deserialized with witness data iff the node requires witness.

Runs before the version handshake. Sets the channel's start_height from query.get_top_confirmed() so the outgoing version message carries the right height to the peer. The base then runs the standard version exchange from libbitcoin-network.
After handshake succeeds, this method decides which P2P protocols run on the channel based on negotiated peer features and node configuration. This is the central network-layer decision tree.

Invariant (Attach-2). protocol_block_in_31800 is attached exactly when the node provides blocks, the peer advertises node_network, and at least headers_protocol is negotiated (:114-131). include/bitcoin/node/protocols/protocol.hpp:33-52: node::protocol does not inherit from network::protocol. Instead, concrete protocols multiply-inherit from network::protocol_peer (the wire-level base) and node::protocol (via node::protocol_peer, protocol_peer.hpp:33-54). The subscribe_chase machinery uses shared_from_sibling to get a shared_ptr<node::protocol> out of a network::protocol& (protocol.cpp:183-195). The base forwards the node surface to the session: organizers (organize, organize_compact, prioritize, get_minimum_work, submit, submit_compact), currency predicates, minimum_fee_rate() (the configured rate when current, max_money otherwise, :74-78), estimate, connection and suspension passthroughs, and channel/address counts (protocol.cpp:34-181).

// src/protocols/protocol.cpp:183-195 void protocol::subscribe_chase(event_notifier&& handler) NOEXCEPT { const auto self = dynamic_cast<network::protocol&>(*this) .shared_from_sibling<node::protocol, network::protocol>(); event_completer completer = std::bind(&protocol::handle_subscribed, self, _1, _2); session_->subscribe_chase(std::move(handler), std::bind(&protocol::handle_subscribe, self, _1, _2, std::move(completer))); } The chain: protocol → session → full_node → posts to node strand → subscribes → completer fires → handle_subscribe stores the key_ → handle_subscribed posts back to channel strand → calls the override subscribed(ec, key) for any protocol-specific init (:197-232). Invariant (Protocol-Sub-1). Each protocol may have at most one active subscription. Enforced by BC_ASSERT_MSG(is_zero(key_), "unsafe access") in handle_subscribe (protocol.cpp:202). Invariant (Protocol-Sub-2). unsubscribe_chase must be called from the protocol's stopping(...) override. The base subscribed calls it on early failure or if the channel already stopped (protocol.cpp:225-232).

node::protocol_peer (src/protocols/protocol_peer.cpp) adds the download-map RPCs (get_hashes/put_hashes), performance, fault (self-stop plus session fault, :53-61), the anti-echo filter accessors set_announced/was_announced (per channel, :66-79), set_current (channel buffer policy, :71-74), event notification, and make_compact_block (BIP152 v2 compact block of an associated block with the coinbase prefilled and short ids over wtxids, :98-134).

Every channel has one. Its jobs (src/protocols/protocol_observer.cpp): Translate chase::suspend to channel stop. When the bus broadcasts suspend, every observer calls stop(ec) with the event's code (:69-94). Result: a suspend event tears down every peer connection. Hygiene: drop peers that send unrequested tx inventories when relay is disallowed (:100-119). Diagnostics: answers network::diagnostics broadcasts with a per-channel row (peer version, services, fee, bytes by message, ping times, :129-189) and network::terminator broadcasts by stopping the targeted channel (:192-210). Invariant (Observer-Suspend-1). A single chase::suspend emission drops all channels via the per-channel observer. The base network::net also suspends its listeners (doc 00 §6.2), so the combined effect is "stop all current and refuse new".

src/protocols/protocol_performer.cpp. A mixin used by protocol_block_in_31800 to drive the speed-reporting cycle. Key code paths: start_performance() (:35-46): start clock, reset byte counter, arm the timer (period node.sample_period_seconds). handle_performance_timer(ec) (:48-76): on tick, if idle ⇒ pause_performance (sends max_uint64); else compute rate in bytes/s and send_performance. send_performance(rate) (:90-113): if deviation_ is enabled, send via the performance(rate, handler) RPC → chaser_download → maybe slow_channel; else only stalled/exhausted detection locally. do_handle_performance(ec) (:123-152): Reply code Reaction exhausted_channel Stop the timer; wait for chase::download to restart stalled_channel, slow_channel stop(ec) — drop the channel other error stop(ec) success start_performance() — go again Invariant (Performer-1). bytes_ is reset at every start_performance, so rate = bytes_/elapsed is bytes/sec since the last tick boundary. Invariant (Performer-2). A channel that returns exhausted_channel is NOT dropped; only the timer is paused. It resumes on the next chase::download event.

This class is the on-the-wire counterpart of chaser_download. The chaser holds the queue of pending downloads (doc 03); this protocol holds one map of in-flight items per channel and shuttles between them.

// protocol_block_in_31800.cpp:370-384 code identify(const chain::view::block& block, const chain::context& ctx, bool bypass) const { if ((ec = block.identify())) return ec; // merkle root, malleation if (bypass && node_pruned_) return success; // stripped block: no witness commitment if ((ec = block.identify(ctx))) return ec; // witness commitment return success; } bypass = query.is_bypass(link) (:289); checked = is_under_checkpoint(height) (:288). Only identity is checked at receive time; block checks are deferred to validation, which allows the simplified view::block here. Invariant (BlockIn-Check-1). Identity failure (invalid_transaction_commitment, invalid_witness_commitment) is interpreted as malleation — stop the peer but do not mark the block unconfirmable (:306-315). A different peer may yet deliver the canonical block. Invariant (BlockIn-Check-2). Any other identity failure ⇒ set_block_unconfirmable(link) is called AND chase::unchecked is emitted (:317-328). chaser_header will then disorganize down to this link (when mark_unconfirmable is set). Invariant (BlockIn-Pruned-1). A pruned node (limited_blocks) requests bypassed blocks without witness (to_block_type, :441-446), rejects a segregated bypassed block (:290-295), skips the witness commitment, and archives bypassed blocks without input scripts (prune = bypass && node_pruned_, :335).

Failure here is a node fault (suspends the network via fault(code)). Invariant (BlockIn-Store-1). A chase::checked(height) event is emitted only after set_code succeeded (:336-352). Emitting chase::starved causes chaser_download::do_starved to either pick the slowest channel and signal a split or — if no channels are tracked — broadcast stall. Invariant (BlockIn-Starve-1). chase::starved is emitted with the protocol's own subscription key (events_key()). The chaser uses this key to avoid asking the starved peer to split its own (empty) work.

The session layer's only consensus-relevant action is the attach tree (§2.3). A spec can model: attach(channel, peer, settings) : Set Protocol = { observer } ∪ filters(...) ∪ block_in_set(...) ∪ block_out_set(...) ∪ tx_set(...) Once start_channel succeeds and attach_protocols runs, the set is fixed for that channel's lifetime.

State: map ∈ MaybeQueue (HashPair), job ∈ MaybeJobBarrier, bytes ∈ ℕ. Inputs (channel strand): peer block messages; bus events listed in §5.3; performance timer ticks. Inputs (chaser strand, via RPC results): handle_get_hashes(ec, map, job), handle_put_hashes(ec, count). Outputs: peer getdata messages; bus events chase::checked, chase::unchecked, chase::starved; store mutations set_code, set_block_unconfirmable.

Store-precedes-bus (BlockIn-Store-1): chase::checked(h) ⇒ the block is durably stored at the link to_candidate(h). No silent invalidation: every chase::unchecked(link) is preceded by a successful set_block_unconfirmable(link). Failure path goes to fault, not silent drop (BlockIn-Check-2). Map ownership: at any time, a given map entry is in exactly one place: in chaser_download.maps_, in some channel's map_, or in flight as a returned restore to the chaser. Job barrier completeness: while any channel holds job_, the chaser's race_all is not complete.

Each channel either keeps progressing (chase::checked per block) or emits chase::starved when its map drains, prompting the chaser to rebalance. A persistently slow channel is dropped via slow_channel; a persistently stuck channel via stalled_channel.

Sessions: the three session subclasses differ only in that enabled is customised for inbound and the connection count for outbound; the attach tree (§2.3) is the only behavioural component. node::protocol sibling pattern: a workaround for C++ multiple inheritance — without that constraint a wire protocol can simply hold a reference to the node. protocol_block_in_31800: an actor with one mailbox for peer messages and one for chaser events. The interleaving on the channel strand makes it inherently single-threaded per channel. protocol_performer: a recurring scheduled task that snapshots bytes_ and computes a rate.

The session layer adds no shared state — it is a static dispatch from configuration + handshake state to a finite protocol set, plus one integer (the outbound target) driven by currency. protocol_block_in_31800 is strand-confined; its only off-strand interactions are get_hashes/put_hashes/performance RPCs which post to the chaser strand. The full system can be modelled as one chaser strand + N independent channel strands communicating only by the bus and these three RPCs. The map-ownership property (§8.3-3) is the non-trivial correctness obligation here; an exchange protocol proof can be modelled with a token-passing semantics.

Companion to 04-chaser-validate, 05-chaser-confirm, 07-header-protocols §4 and 10-tx-protocols. chaser_transaction owns the unconfirmed transaction pool. The pool is an index over archived transactions: a submitted transaction is validated, archived in the store like any other tx, and marked pooled under the context of the next block. There is no separate mempool data structure; "pooled" is a store property, and the pool contents outlive the process. The chaser: validates and archives submitted packages (submit), emitting chase::transaction per newly pooled tx; fills identified compact blocks from the pool (submit_compact), validating and archiving the unpooled txs in block order, associating the block, and emitting chase::checked — the second archiver of blocks after protocol_block_in_31800; re-pools the unpooled txs of a reorganized block; maintains the pool context on every organized block, closes the pool when the chain is not current, and maps silent-payment scan starts on a dedicated single thread. Source: do_submit :257-333. Parents precede children in a package, so a parent is archived before its child is resolved. Per-tx validation (validate(tx), :559-579): tx.check(); tx.check(pool_) // tx consensus archive().populate_with_metadata(tx, true, true) // external prevouts from confirmed and pooled tx.accept(pool_) tx.check_guard(); tx.check_guard(pool_); tx.accept_guard(pool_); tx.confirm_guard(pool_) // presumed block rules (DoS guard) tx.connect(pool_) // scripts last, most costly Invariant (Pool-Validate-1). A pooled tx has passed tx consensus, the block-level rules it would be subject to in the next block (the guards), and script validation, all under the pool context. The pooled block path of chaser_validate relies on this to skip per-tx validation (doc 04 §4.2). Invariant (Pool-Package-1). A package is accepted or rejected as a whole, by validation; archival is per tx in order, so a disk-full decline can leave a package partly archived, which a resubmit resolves (:306-310).

do_submit_compact(txs, links, link) (:336-417) receives the unpooled txs of an identified compact block and the full link vector with terminal entries at their positions: duplicate_block if the block is already associated (another channel filled it); transaction3 fault if the context is missing; transaction5 if the terminal count does not match the tx count. Each terminal position is filled in block order by fill (:435-487): an already stored tx (matched by witness, to_stored) is reused and, if pooling and not yet pooled or confirmed, validated under the block context and pooled; an unstored tx is validated under the block context, archived (set_code), pooled unless coinbase, and silent indexed when at or above silent_start_height under taproot. Each newly pooled tx emits chase::transaction. The coinbase, when missing, is filled last (validation indexes only txs linked above it). query.set_code(link, filled, strong) associates the block with strong = is_under_checkpoint(height); then chase::checked. A tx that fails validation makes the identified block unconfirmable: unconfirmable (:490-500) sets the block unconfirmable (transaction4 on failure), emits chase::unchecked and returns the consensus code to the protocol, which drops the peer. Block-context tx validation (validate(tx, ctx), :583-596) applies check, check(ctx), populate_with_metadata, accept(ctx), connect(ctx) — no policy (fee rate, guards), because a block tx is under proof of work and may conflict with unconfirmed txs. Invariant (Pool-Compact-1). A compact-filled block is associated only after every one of its txs is archived and (for unpooled ones) validated under the block's own context, in block order. chase::checked then carries the same guarantee as the download path (doc 06 §5.6): the block is durably associated before the event. Invariant (Pool-Compact-2). Block checks are deferred: the txs given to submit_compact are an arbitrary subset of the block, so block-level rules run in chaser_validate (the pooled path when all txs are sufficiently pooled, else full validation).

do_reorganized(link) (:193-232) recomputes the pool context, then for every non-coinbase tx of the popped block that is neither pooled nor confirmed by another block, populates it with metadata and pools it under the block's context with the block's timestamp as arrival time, emitting chase::transaction. Block txs are already silent indexed. Invariant (Pool-Reorg-1). No transaction of a reorganized block is lost: it is either confirmed elsewhere, already pooled, or re-pooled by this handler.

When the store's silent index is enabled, the chaser builds and maintains the scan start map — the per-block entry points that the server's silent-payment scans use — on the single-thread scan_threadpool_ (start_scan/do_scan/do_scanned, :155-189): a full map (remap = true) when genesis has no scan start; an extension when the top has none and the pool is not yet latched; a remap when the top is unmapped and the top's coinbase precedes the pool latch tx (rows of a block archived before the latch may precede mapped starts). The map is bounded by the scan frontier once pooling. Blocks organized during a map are mapped by the do_bump that do_scanned re-runs. Invariant (Pool-Scan-1). Scan starts are mapped only after the pool latch, since pooled rows are unordered; at most one map runs at a time (scanning_), and a failed map is a transaction8 fault.

Sends feefilter{ minimum_fee_rate() } at start and whenever chase::block or chase::stale changes the answer (:42-52, :58-69, :71-93): the configured rate while current, max_money while not (protocol::minimum_fee_rate, doc 06 §3). This is how currency is signalled to peers. Records the peer's feefilter on the channel (set_minimum_fee, :98-108). do_announce skips txs whose rate is below the peer's filter (is_filtered, :113-148); a missing fee record is a store integrity fault. Invariant (TxOut-Fee-1). A peer is never sent an announcement below the rate it advertised, and is told max_money whenever the node is not current, so the node receives no relay while catching up.

Companion to 00-overview, 01-event-bus, 02-chaser-header, 03-chaser-download. chaser_validate is the consensus pre-check stage. For each block on the candidate chain (in heights-first order): it ensures the block is downloaded (chase::checked already received) it chooses one of three paths: pooled (every tx already validated in the pool, only block checks run), bypass (under checkpoint or milestone: only the optional filter / silent-payment indexes are produced from a read-only view), or full (populate, block.check, block.accept, block.connect) signatures captured during connect may be committed to a store-side batch bank and verified later in bulk (CPU or GPU); the block is marked valid only when its bank drains silent-payment rows may likewise be banked and computed in bulk it emits chase::valid(height) on success or chase::unvalid(link) on failure This is the chaser most directly relevant to formal verification: it is where script execution and prevout (UTXO availability) checks happen before confirmation. Consensus is not confined to this chaser however — it is split across several stages: Headers (chaser_header::validate, run by the header protocols) — context-free header consensus plus limited-context checks. Blocks at receive time (protocol_block_in_31800::identify) — only identity: merkle and witness commitments, malleation. This chaser — block checks and full block consensus with prevouts populated: block.check, block.accept(ctx, …) (block-wide rules) and block.connect(ctx) (script execution per input), or the pooled equivalent in the store. chaser_confirm — block-relative order-based consensus checks via query.block_confirmable(link) (see 05 §11.4). Transactions (chaser_transaction::validate) — tx consensus and policy for pooled transactions, which the pooled block path relies on. There is no longer a defer-validation setting and the chaser is always active.

Bypass is a stored header property, read as database::is_bypass(state) (:230): the block is under the top checkpoint or was archived under the active milestone (doc 07 §2.3). Invariant (Validate-Bypass-1). Under bypass: - block.check, block.accept, block.connect are not run. - query.set_prevouts(link, block) is not called. - the block is read as a chain::view::block and only its optional indexes are produced (validate_view, §4.2). set_block_valid is written on the bypass path (complete_view, chaser_validate_parallel.cpp:197-210), after set_filter_body. This is the only place where consensus checks can be elided; it is gated on checkpoint/milestone — the rest of the system must trust that these gates are sound. A bypassed block that needs no index at all (no filters and not silent-eligible) is completed on the strand without posting (chaser_validate.cpp:250-253).
2. Concurrency model — unique among the chasers

chaser_validate is the only chaser with its own thread pool. // chaser_validate.hpp:163-166, chaser_validate.cpp:39-41, :393-401 network::threadpool validation_threadpool_; // node.threads, node.thread_priority network::io::strand validation_strand_; // on validation_threadpool_ strand() → validation_strand_ // overrides base stranded() → validation_strand_.running_in_this_thread() Method Runs on handle_chase (bus callback) node strand (POSTs to the validation strand; windowed and resume drain inline) do_bump, do_bumped, do_checked, do_regressed, post_block, post_scan, do_purge_capture validation strand validate_block, scan_block, populate, validate, validate_view, validate_pooled validation threadpool (any worker) — one job per block in flight complete_block, notify_block whichever thread finished the block, or the strand process_batch, process_silent_batch any thread that observes a mature bank; at most one drains at a time The strand serialises admission; the pool parallelises execution; batch drains are self-serviced by whichever thread completes the work that matured the bank. maximum_backlog_ caps in-flight parallelism.

// chaser_validate.cpp:374-391 void stopping(const code& ec) { stopping_.store(true); validation_threadpool_.stop(); chaser::stopping(ec); } void stop() { if (!validation_threadpool_.join()) std::abort(); } stopping_ is a stopper observed by the batch kernels so long-running GPU/CPU verification cancels (do_process_batch, :103, :111). Invariant (Validate-Lifecycle-1). All posted validate_block jobs and any running batch drain must complete or cancel before stop() returns. The threadpool's join enforces the former; the stopping_ cancel token and the closed() checks in the drain loops the latter.

Self-bump on backlog drain (chaser_validate.cpp:284-289) prevents validation from stalling when the loop guard would otherwise sit idle. From a spec standpoint it is equivalent to a bus-mediated chase::bump; treat it as such.

Pooled (validate_pooled / complete_pooled, :212-248). Only for current non-bypass blocks. query.validate_pooled(link, ctx, subsidy…) runs the block-level checks in the store over txs that are all already pooled under a sufficient context (doc 11 §4). database::error::unvalidated means "not all pooled, fall through to full"; other store codes are validate11 faults; consensus codes mark the block unconfirmable. On success the block is marked scanned (pooled txs were silent-indexed on entry) and valid, producing a filter body first if filters are enabled. Bypass (validate_view / complete_view, :164-210). The block is read as a chain::view::block over the wire bytes, with witness only when the node requires witness and the block is silent-eligible. Prevouts are populated for all inputs when a filter is produced, otherwise only for silent-payment eligible txs. set_filter_body (when enabled) and the silent index (direct, or banked) are written, then set_block_valid. missing_previous_output marks the block unconfirmable. Full (populate + validate, :134-147, :250-304): // populate block.populate(ctx) // internal prevouts, maturity and time locks query.populate_with_metadata(block) // external prevouts + spent-coin metadata, else missing_previous_output // validate block.check(false); block.check(ctx, false) // (a) block checks (deferred from download) block.accept(ctx, subsidy_interval_, initial_subsidy_) // (b) block-wide consensus capture = get_capture(link); capturing = capture.enabled // signature capture when batching and not current ec = block.connect(ctx, capture) // (c) script execution; batched = capture.batched if capturing: batched ? commit_capture(batched, link) : clear_capture() query.set_prevouts(link, block) → validate7 // (d) persist prevout metadata for confirmation query.set_filter_body(link, block) → validate8 // (e) BIP158 body if silent-eligible: commit_silent_batch or set_silent → validate9 if !batched: query.set_block_valid(link) → validate10 // (f) deferred when batched Invariant (Validate-Populate-1). Every input not satisfied by internal-block prevouts must be satisfied by the store, otherwise populate returns missing_previous_output. This is the UTXO availability check. Invariant (Validate-Ordering-1). set_prevouts precedes set_filter_body, and set_block_valid follows both (chaser_validate_parallel.cpp:286-302). The store represents block state as monotone flags; setting valid before metadata is complete would expose confirmation to an incomplete record. Under batching, the valid flag is written by the drain (mark_valids), after the signatures verified.

Three terminal cases plus the batch hooks (chaser_validate.cpp:281-348): if backlog == 0 and not stranded: self-bump node-category error → fault(ec) // validate1..12, batch* other error → notify_block(ec) → chase::unvalid success and not batched → notify_block(success) → chase::valid success and batched → nothing yet; the drain will notify then: silent drain when recent or residual; signature drain when batched/current/residual; POST(do_purge_capture) once current (release accumulator slabs) Invariant (Validate-Complete-1). Each validate_block invocation produces exactly one of: a fault, a chase::unvalid, a chase::valid now, or a chase::valid/unvalid later from the drain of its bank (mark_valids/mark_invalids). Node-category errors are always faults; a signature failure found at drain time is reported as system::error::invalid_signature.

Script execution dominates validation cost, and most of it is ECDSA and Schnorr verification. During catch-up (non-current headers) the node captures each signature check instead of performing it, commits the rows to a store-side table, and verifies them later in bulk — on a GPU when present, otherwise on the CPU when cpu_batch_verify is set. Silent-payment index rows are banked the same way (cpu_batch_silent, batch_silent), independent of signatures. Capturing is disabled for current headers (get_capture, chaser_validate_capture.cpp:68-80), so a current block always completes by the direct path.

Each batch has two banks in the store. Commits (commit_capture, commit_silent_batch) enter the bank selected by an atomic bank_ and count themselves in writers_[bank]; a drain flips bank_ so new commits go to the other bank, then spins until writers_[old] is zero before reading it (enter_capture/exit_capture, process_batch, chaser_validate_batch.cpp:58-115, :459-494). Invariant (Validate-Bank-1). A writer admitted to a bank that is then switched retries on the other bank (enter_capture loop), so a drain observes every writer of its bank and never reads a partially written commit. Invariant (Validate-Bank-2). At most one drain runs at a time per batch (draining_.exchange(true)); losers return and rely on the winner, which retests maturity after each drain so commits that lost the claim are drained too.

A bank drains when mature — its row count reached batch_verify / batch_silent — or when a residual drain is forced (is_mature, is_silent_mature, chaser_validate_batch.cpp:238-273, :281-293). A residual drain is allowed whenever the backlog is empty and either the download window is fully archived (window_archived_, set by chase::windowed) or the maximum height has been posted (is_residual, :250-255); complete_block also forces one for the first current block so that nothing is left banked when the chain becomes current.

do_process_batch(bank, startup) (:118-176): query.verify_ecdsa_signatures(cancel, use_gpu, fails, bank) and query.verify_schnorr_signatures(...); each returns the links of blocks with a failed signature; cancellation returns operation_canceled. mark_invalids: each failed block is set unconfirmable and reported with chase::unvalid(invalid_signature) (:189-214). mark_valids: every remaining prevalid block is set valid in parallel (poolstl par) and reported with chase::valid (:218-244). purge_batch: prevalids before signatures (:178-187). A silent bank drains with query.compute_silents(cancel, use_gpu, bank), purges presilents then silents, and emits chase::bump because the bank's blocks may now be confirmable (:386-418). Confirmation gates on the scanned flag, so a block whose silent rows are still banked is not yet in the validated fork (doc 05 §4). Invariant (Validate-Batch-1). A block is marked valid under batching only after every signature it captured has been verified, and a block with any failed signature is marked unconfirmable and never valid (mark_invalids replaces its link with terminal before mark_valids). Invariant (Validate-Batch-2). A store decline on commit (e.g. disk full) never loses validity: the captured rows are verified in place by commit_capture (chaser_validate_capture.cpp:102-127) and the block completes by the non-batched path; the decline is faulted as batch5 (recoverable). The same holds for silent rows (batch6, commit_silent_).

Batch state is the store, so a crash or shutdown mid-bank loses nothing: start_batch / start_silent_batch drain any non-empty bank before the chaser subscribes (chaser_validate_batch.cpp:41-56, :315-329). A validated block whose silent bank was dropped by a store restore is re-scanned by post_scan (chaser_validate.cpp:231-248).

do_bumped (chaser_validate.cpp:206-264) is the inner work-finder. For each iteration: Compute link = to_candidate(height); fetch get_block_state(link). If not associated → return (the gap; nothing more to do). If height == maximum_height_ latch maximum_posted_. If unconfirmable → return (chain top is bad; halt). Branch on the flags: validated and scanned → complete inline with success (advances position; happens after restart or regression) validated, not scanned, banks non-empty → process_silent_batch(true) and return (its bank will scan it and bump) validated, not scanned, banks empty → post_scan (bank dropped by restore) bypass and no index needed → complete inline with success otherwise → post_block(link, bypass) set_position(height++). Invariant (Validate-Iter-1). position_ increases monotonically in do_bumped, regardless of path. Each iteration that doesn't early-exit advances by one. Invariant (Validate-Iter-2). Encountering an unassociated state aborts the loop (:220-221). This guarantees that no block is bypassed-as-valid without being downloaded first — there's no path through the loop that writes a valid flag on an unassociated link.

do_checked(h) (:179-186): if h == position+1, call do_bumped(h). This is the fast path for when a block arrives right at the head — skip waiting for the next chase::bump. do_bump (:188-201): if recovering from disk full and the backlog is empty, reset the position to the fork point (in-flight blocks were lost to the full disk); then do_bumped if the next height is validateable. do_regressed(bp) (:170-177): if bp < position, set position to bp. The next bump re-walks from there. Crucially, there is no purge like in chaser_download: in-flight validations on heights above bp keep running. Their results either find the block still on the candidate chain (rare) or not (typical); either way the work itself is correct and the only "wasted" output is bus traffic. Invariant (Validate-Regress-1). A regression does not invalidate in-flight validations. Their results are persisted via set_block_valid(link) only if validation succeeds; the store reconciles correctness via the link/state map.

Spec obligation list. Each validateN/batchN should be proved unreachable under the store-consistency invariants supplied by libbitcoin-database, combined with the strand and bank discipline: - validate2, validate3: a block whose state was read as associated has a context and a body. - validate4, validate5, validate12: set_block_unconfirmable failure implies store I/O failure. - validate7–validate10: each is a store-write that "should not fail given previous reads succeeded". - validate11: the pooled query is consistent with the pool state. - batch1–batch4, batch7, batch8: bank reads and purges are consistent under the turnstile (Validate-Bank-1). - batch5, batch6: declines are recoverable by construction (Validate-Batch-2).

chaser_validate is a process with: inputs: bus events listed in §3 outputs: bus events chase::valid, chase::unvalid, chase::bump; store mutations state: position_ ∈ ℕ, backlog ∈ [0, maximum_backlog_], the latches disk_recovering, window_archived, maximum_posted, and per batch: bank ∈ {A, B}, writers[A|B] ∈ ℕ, draining ∈ 𝔹 internal jobs: bounded number (≤ maximum_backlog_) of pending per-block tasks, plus at most one drain per batch

Safety No validation without download (Validate-Iter-2): for every chase::valid(h), the block at link to_candidate(h) has previously been associated. Bypass discipline (Validate-Bypass-1): no script execution and no prevout metadata under bypass; the store distinguishes "validated" from "bypassed" by the bypass flag. Ordering (Validate-Ordering-1): set_block_valid after set_prevouts and set_filter_body, and after batch verification. Exactly one outcome per block (Validate-Complete-1). Batch soundness (Validate-Batch-1): valid implies every captured signature verified. Liveness Provided chaser_download keeps issuing downloads and the store responds, every height on the candidate chain eventually receives a complete_block call. Backlog drain self-bump (Validate-Backlog-2) and the inline windowed drain (Validate-Drain-1) prevent stalls when the strand is saturated or the last blocks of a window are banked.

validate : (block, ctx, bypass, current) → {valid, unvalid(reason), fault(code)} if current ∧ all txs pooled under sufficient context: store.validate_pooled(link, ctx) > ok -- block checks only [filter body]; set scanned; set valid; succeed elif bypass: view.populate(selected prevouts) > ok [filter body]; [silent index]; set valid; succeed else: block.populate(ctx) > ok query.populate_with_metadata(block) > ok block.check; block.check(ctx) > ok block.accept(ctx, subsidy_interval, initial_subsidy) > ok block.connect(ctx, capture) > ok -- signatures captured when batching set_prevouts; set_filter_body; [silent index] batched ? (valid when the bank verifies) : set valid; succeed The libbitcoin-system functions (block.accept, block.connect, the signature kernels) and the store queries (validate_pooled, verify_*_signatures, compute_silents) are the actual consensus rules. They are external to this chaser and deserve their own specification; this chaser only sequences and persists their outcomes.

The strand/loop pattern (one strand, many workers, atomic backlog) maps to a typed actor with a bounded mailbox and a worker pool. Batching is a performance feature; validate_block with capturing disabled is the reference behaviour, and a store decline on commit falls back to exactly that. The bank/turnstile protocol is lock-free: two atomics per batch (bank_, draining_) and two writer counters. The draining worker yields only until in-flight commits to its bank complete; arriving commits go to the other bank and losing claimants return, so every other thread continues. A model can use an epoch counter. The store interface used by validate is wide; see the coupling diagram.

Off-strand parallelism makes this the only chaser that needs more than single-threaded reasoning. The shared variables are the atomic validate_backlog_, the three latches, and the batch state; the strand serialises everything else. A proof outline: treat each posted validate_block as an independent process that does not read or write position_ except for the final fetch_sub and the batch commit under the turnstile. Then the strand and the workers commute except at those points. The hard part of a consensus proof is in libbitcoin-system and the store kernels; this chaser only proves that their outputs are persisted in the right order and the right state transitions emitted, including across a bank drain and across a restart.

Architecture of libbitcoin-server: the server node, interface sessions, channels and protocols, requests, responses and notifications. Bitcoin Server (bs) is a full node with client interfaces. The library libbitcoin-server extends the libbitcoin-node full node, which owns the store and the chasers, with one network service per client interface. Each service is a session that accepts connections, a channel type for the connection, and a set of protocols that dispatch requests, query the store and push notifications from chain events. The wire API of each interface is documented under Interfaces; this page describes the structure that serves them. Paths are relative to include/bitcoin/server/ in libbitcoin-server, at master f97e9b10 (2026-10-27).

server_node derives node::full_node (server_node.hpp). It adds the server configuration and overrides do_run, so that the client services start only after the node is running. Each service is attached and started in turn, each start completing into the next: void server_node::start_admin(const code& ec, const result_handler& handler) NOEXCEPT { if (ec) { handler(ec); return; } attach_admin_session()->start(std::bind(&server_node::start_native, this, _1, handler)); } The order is admin, native, bitcoind, btcd, electrum, sparrow, esplora, stratum v1, stratum v2 and ZMQ. Each attach_*_session() is virtual, and constructs its session from the server configuration and the service's own settings section (for example config_.server.electrum).

server::session derives node::session (sessions/session.hpp). It holds the server configuration and exposes, through the node, address pool counts and dumps, channel byte totals, and the wire tx and block demand counters. session_server<Protocols...> derives server::session and network::session_server (sessions/session_server.hpp). The network base manages connections: accept, start, stop, enable, and the black and white lists. The first protocol of the pack declares channel_t and options_t, which fix the channel and settings types of the session, and each accepted connection gets every protocol of the pack, attached and started in order: channel_ptr create_channel(const socket_ptr& socket) NOEXCEPT override { return std::make_shared<channel_t>(log, socket, create_key(), node_config(), options_); } void attach_protocols(const channel_ptr& channel) NOEXCEPT override { const auto self = shared_from_base<session_server<Protocols...>>(); ((channel->attach<Protocols>(self, options_)->start(), void()), ...); } session_handshake<Handshake, Protocols...> adds one handshake protocol, which completes before the others are attached (sessions/session_handshake.hpp). A session drops inbound connections until the confirmed chain is current if its first protocol is delayed and the node's delay_inbound is set (enabled()). server::protocol sets delayed; protocol_admin clears it.

All sessions are aliases (sessions/sessions.hpp): Session Protocols Channel Settings session_admin protocol_admin channel_html admin session_native protocol_native channel_html native session_bitcoind protocol_bitcoind_rest, subgroups, protocol_bitcoind channel_bitcoind bitcoind session_btcd protocol_btcd, subgroups, protocol_bitcoind channel_btcd btcd session_electrum handshake protocol_electrum_version, protocol_electrum channel_electrum electrum session_sparrow handshake protocol_electrum_version, protocol_sparrow channel_electrum sparrow session_esplora protocol_esplora channel_html esplora session_stratum_v1 protocol_stratum_v1 channel_stratum_v1 stratum_v1 session_stratum_v2 protocol_stratum_v2 channel_stratum_v2 stratum_v2 session_zmq protocol_zmq channel_zmq zmq The bitcoind subgroups are blockchain, control, mining, network, notifications, test, transaction, utility and wallet, each a protocol with its own dispatcher (protocol_bitcoind_dispatch<Interface>).

A channel is one connection. Server channels derive server::channel, which derives node::channel (channels/channel.hpp), and the network channel of their transport: Channel Base Role channel_http network::channel_http HTTP base; a service preselects its reader body (default_body) channel_html channel_http Plain text body: admin, native, esplora channel_rpc channel_http JSON-RPC over TCP (by downgrade), HTTP and WebSocket (by upgrade); the senders channel_bitcoind channel_rpc bitcoind channel_btcd channel_bitcoind Authorized in-band, so the WebSocket upgrade is open channel_electrum channel_rpc Negotiated version and client name channel_stratum_v1 network::channel_rpc Non-HTTP JSON-RPC channel_stratum_v2 network::channel Binary channel_zmq network::channel_rpc ZMTP publisher State of the connection is held by the channel. channel_electrum holds the version that the handshake negotiates and protocol_electrum reads (at_least), and normalizes each request's parameters for that version before dispatch.

server::protocol derives node::protocol (protocols/protocol.hpp), from which it inherits the store query (archive()), transaction submission (submit) and the event subscription (subscribe_chase). protocol_http adds WebSocket dispatch (dispatch_websocket). protocol_html adds GET dispatch, trying an interface object, then local files, then the embedded pages. protocol_rpc<Interface> adds the interface dispatcher, POST and WebSocket dispatch, and the JSON-RPC senders. protocol_bitcoind_dispatch does the same for a bitcoind subgroup.

All protocols attached to a channel receive each request. A latch on the channel (claimed(), set_claimed()) gives each request to one of them. A protocol whose interface defines the method claims and dispatches it, and one whose interface does not defers it to handle_unclaimed (protocols/protocol_rpc.hpp): if (claimed()) return; if (!rpc_dispatcher::contains(message.method)) { handle_unclaimed(message); return; } set_claimed(); if (const auto code = rpc_dispatcher_.notify(message)) stop(code); The protocol attached last is the terminal responder, overriding handle_unclaimed to reply method-not-found: protocol_bitcoind in the bitcoind and btcd sessions, protocol_electrum in the electrum session. protocol_sparrow derives protocol_electrum and tries its own dispatcher in handle_unclaimed before deferring to electrum; protocol_btcd adds its dispatcher to protocol_bitcoind in the same way. An electrum response that sparrow extends is overridden, not reimplemented (add_features for server.features).

An interface is a compile-time tuple of methods, each a name with typed parameters, constructed with the parameter names (interfaces/). Optional parameters carry their defaults in the type (optional<0.0>, optional<false>, optional<""_t>). The Electrum interface, condensed (interfaces/electrum.hpp): struct electrum_methods { /// Methods (electrum protocol versions 1.0-1.7). static constexpr std::tuple methods { method<"blockchain.numblocks.subscribe">{}, method<"blockchain.block.header", number_t, optional<0.0>>{ "height", "cp_height" }, method<"blockchain.block.headers", number_t, number_t, optional<0.0>>{ "start_height", "count", "cp_height" }, method<"blockchain.headers.subscribe", optional<false>>{ "raw" }, // ... method<"blockchain.scripthash.get_balance", string_t>{ "scripthash" }, method<"blockchain.scripthash.subscribe", string_t>{ "scripthash" }, // ... method<"blockchain.transaction.get", string_t, optional<false>>{ "tx_hash", "verbose" }, // ... method<"server.ping", optional<0.0>, optional<""_t>>{ "pong_len", "data" }, method<"mempool.get_fee_histogram">{}, // ... }; }; Each method is also named as a type, which tags its handler. The REST interfaces take the same form, their parameters parsed from the URL, with the API version and response media leading and nullable parameters for alternatives such as a block by hash or by height (interfaces/native.hpp): struct native_methods { static constexpr std::tuple methods { method<"top", uint8_t, uint8_t>{ "version", "media" }, method<"block_header", uint8_t, uint8_t, nullable<system::hash_cptr>, nullable<uint32_t>>{ "version", "media", "hash", "height" }, method<"tx", uint8_t, uint8_t, system::hash_cptr, optional<true>>{ "version", "media", "hash", "witness" }, // ... }; }; A protocol holds a network::rpc::dispatcher<Interface> and subscribes one handler per method when it starts (src/protocols/electrum/protocol_electrum.cpp): SUBSCRIBE_RPC(handle_blockchain_block_header, _1, _2, _3, _4); SUBSCRIBE_RPC(handle_blockchain_scripthash_get_balance, _1, _2, _3); The dispatcher converts a request's parameters to the declared types, by name or by position, and invokes the handler with them. Each handler takes the method's tag type and then its typed parameters (protocols/protocol_electrum.hpp, protocols/protocol_native.hpp): void handle_blockchain_block_header(const code& ec, rpc_interface::blockchain_block_header, double height, double cp_height) NOEXCEPT; void handle_blockchain_scripthash_get_balance(const code& ec, rpc_interface::blockchain_scripthash_get_balance, const std::string& scripthash) NOEXCEPT; bool handle_get_block_header(const code& ec, interface::block_header, uint8_t version, uint8_t media, std::optional<system::hash_cptr> hash, std::optional<uint32_t> height) NOEXCEPT; A request whose method is not in the interface, or whose parameters do not convert, is answered with an error without reaching a handler. The protocol's handlers are therefore exactly the interface's methods, each with its declared signature, checked by the compiler. JSON-RPC requests arrive as a request model from the channel's body reader. The REST interfaces parse the URL into the same model (network::rpc::request_t) and dispatch it the same way (parsers/): Parser Produces native_target, native_query Native method and parameters from path and query; get_media selects the response media admin_target, admin_query Admin method and parameters bitcoind_target, bitcoind_query bitcoind REST method and parameters esplora_target Esplora method and parameters electrum_request Electrum parameters normalized for the negotiated version parse_transaction, expand_scan_object, btcd::filter_keys Typed values from structured bitcoind and btcd arguments In protocol_native, a target that does not parse as a method falls through to page dispatch, as does a request for HTML media.

Response construction that is shared or substantial is factored out of the protocols as free functions (serializers/): bitcoind models built from store queries (chain_info, raw_mempool, mempool_entry, deployment_info, block_stats, scan_result), PSBT decoding, and context injectors (inject_block_context, inject_tx_context, inject_tx_prevouts). btcd::search_transaction extends the bitcoind transaction model. Helpers shared with the parsers are in utilities/: address and script conversion, descriptors, PSBT combination and update, median time, fee histogram and merkle proofs. Each interface family has its own error codes (error/): error_t for URL parse and general codes, and bitcoind, btcd and electrum codes. Node and store codes are mapped to the interface's codes at the response (for example translate(ec, daemon_error) in electrum).

A request handler runs on the channel strand. It validates its arguments, moves the store query to the network threadpool (PARALLEL), and posts the result back to the strand (POST) to send it: void protocol_electrum::get_balance(const hash_digest& hash) NOEXCEPT { PARALLEL(do_get_balance, hash, gate()); } void protocol_electrum::do_get_balance(const hash_digest& hash, const gate_t::ptr& gate) NOEXCEPT { uint64_t confirmed{}, unconfirmed{}; const auto ec = archive().get_balance(stopping_, confirmed, unconfirmed, hash); POST(complete_get_balance, ec, confirmed, unconfirmed, gate); } The query is the node's node::query, so a protocol reads the store directly. A method that depends on an optional index checks it first (archive().address_enabled()). A broadcast calls the node protocol's submit, which validates and archives the package, or only validates it when testing.

A protocol that pushes notifications subscribes to the node event bus at start (subscribe_chase) and unsubscribes when stopping. The handler runs off the channel strand, switches on the event (node::to_chase), reads only atomic subscription flags, and posts the work with the event's link (for example POST(do_header, top.link) on organized): Protocol Events protocol_native block, reorganized, transaction protocol_electrum transaction, organized, reorganized protocol_sparrow transaction, organized, then electrum's protocol_btcd organized, reorganized, transaction protocol_bitcoind_blockchain organized, reorganized protocol_zmq organized, transaction, reorganized protocol_admin subscribes to the logger instead, for its log and event streams. Notifications require a full duplex transport (WebSocket or TCP downgrade). The events and their payloads are described in the node event bus.

Each channel has a strand, and protocol handlers run on it (each asserts stranded()). Store queries run on the network threadpool and return their results through POST, so protocol state is touched only on the strand. protocol_electrum and protocol_btcd hold a second strand on the same threadpool (notification_strand_, posted with POST_NOTIFY). Their address and outpoint subscription maps are protected by it, so that notification work is serialized apart from request handling. Settings are constant after initialization and are read from any thread.

server::settings holds one section per service (settings.hpp). Each section derives a network server settings type (http_server, websocket_server, tls_server or zmtp_server), which supplies binds, TLS, connection limits and HTTP or WebSocket options. Derived interfaces derive their settings: btcd_server derives bitcoind_server, and sparrow_server derives electrum_server. Service sections add interface limits (for example maximum_history and maximum_subscriptions) and identity (for example server_name). The wallet section holds the address prefixes used to parse and render addresses. An html_server serves the pages embedded in bs (embedded_pages), or a local directory (path). server::configuration derives node::configuration, adding the server and log settings and the command line actions (configuration.hpp). server::parser loads command line options and configuration file sections into configured, then derives unconfigured hashmap bucket counts (derive_buckets) and the default port of each service bind (derive_ports) (parser.hpp). configuration::initialize then reads files and packs derived settings.

bs is the console application in console/. main builds the parser with the embedded admin and native pages, parses and initializes the configuration, and either runs as an operating system service or calls executor::dispatch (console/main.cpp). dispatch runs one command line action (help, backup, restore, daemon, hardware, flags, new store, buckets, collisions, information, settings, version), or runs the node if none is given (console/executor_commands.cpp). To run, the executor opens the log and event sinks, opens or creates the store (restoring from a snapshot after an unclean close), reports the store and hardware, and prompts on warnings (console/executor_runner.cpp). It then constructs server_node over the store's query and starts it; start completes into run, which starts the client services (console/executor.cpp). On a stop signal it closes the node, then the store. While running, console input is read as single-letter commands (console/executor_options.cpp): b backup, c close, e store errors, g and h go and hold network communication, i store info, m menu, w work distribution and z zeroize a disk full error, plus one toggle key per log level.
Interfaces — the wire API of each interface. Node architecture — the full node and chasers that the server extends. Event bus — the events that drive notifications.

The chain types (chain/) are the block, header, transaction, input, output, script, operation and witness. Each implements the consensus rules that apply to it, and blocks and transactions delegate to their parts. Paths are relative to include/bitcoin/system/ in libbitcoin-system, at master 0585b079 (2026-11-03).

The consensus rules are implemented by the chain types, divided into validation stages by what each needs. The rules of BIP54, which is proposed, are shown in blue. Stage Requires Rules header::check() Proof of work, future timestamp header::accept(context) Version, median time past, work required, time warp (BIP94, BIP54), timespan (BIP54) block::check() Empty block, size, coinbase position and count, forward references, internal double spends, merkle root, empty transactions, coinbase script size, null previous outputs block::check(context) Weight (BIP141), coinbase height (BIP34), transaction size (BIP54), coinbase locktime (BIP54), witness commitment (BIP141), signet solution, absolute locktime (BIP113) block::accept(context) Prevout values Coinbase value against subsidy and fees, sigop limit, missing previous outputs, spends exceeding value, transaction sigop limit (BIP54) block::connect(context) Prevout scripts Script execution of each input, including signatures block::confirm(context) Prevout metadata Coinbase collision (BIP30), relative locktime (BIP68), unconfirmed spends, coinbase maturity, confirmed double spends The division lets a node run each stage as soon as what it requires exists: check a block when it has it, accept and connect it once its previous outputs are available, for many blocks at once, and confirm it in chain order. The node performs the confirmation rules as store queries. See Node Architecture. These stages contain every consensus rule, including script evaluation, which connect performs through the machine. One rule is outside of them: chain organization, the selection among valid chains. Competing branches, valid chains seen in isolation by different nodes, are each perfectly valid in the scope of the node that sees it. The rule of most cumulative proof of work applies only to break what would otherwise be a tie between two valid chains. A node that sees two chains of the same work generally prefers the first seen, but that choice is arbitrary, and in some situations not applied. To compare chains, the node uses the cumulative work of each header. Each stage is a method of the chain type it applies to, and each lists its consensus rules in order, one predicate per rule, each returning its own error code. A block stage applies its block rules, then delegates to the same stage of each transaction (check_transactions, and so on). The sources below are from src/chain/header.cpp, src/chain/block.cpp and src/chain/transaction.cpp.

A header is checked alone, then accepted in its context: code header::check() const NOEXCEPT { if (is_invalid_proof_of_work()) return error::invalid_proof_of_work; if (is_futuristic_timestamp()) return error::futuristic_timestamp; return error::block_success; } code header::accept(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { ⁣ const auto bip54_timespan = ctx.is_enabled(bip54_timespan_rule);⁤ ⁣⁤ if (is_insufficient_version(ctx)) return error::insufficient_block_version; if (is_anachronistic_timestamp(ctx)) return error::anachronistic_timestamp; if (is_invalid_work(ctx)) return error::incorrect_proof_of_work; if (is_early_timestamp(ctx)) return error::early_timestamp; ⁣ if (bip54_timespan && is_negative_timespan(ctx))⁤ ⁣ return error::negative_timespan;⁤ return error::block_success; }

The rules of the block alone: code block::check() const NOEXCEPT { if (is_empty()) return error::empty_block; if (is_oversized()) return error::block_size_limit; if (is_first_non_coinbase()) return error::first_not_coinbase; if (is_extra_coinbases()) return error::extra_coinbases; if (is_forward_reference()) return error::forward_reference; if (is_internal_double_spend()) return error::block_internal_double_spend; if (is_invalid_merkle_root()) return error::invalid_transaction_commitment; return check_transactions(); } code transaction::check() const NOEXCEPT { const auto coinbase = is_coinbase(); if (is_empty()) return error::empty_transaction; if (coinbase && is_invalid_coinbase_size()) return error::invalid_coinbase_script_size; if (!coinbase && is_null_non_coinbase()) return error::previous_output_null; return error::transaction_success; }

The rules that depend on the block's height and active forks, but not on previous outputs: code block::check(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { const auto bip141 = ctx.is_enabled(bip141_rule); const auto bip34 = ctx.is_enabled(bip34_rule); ⁣ const auto bip54_txsize = ctx.is_enabled(bip54_txsize_rule);⁤ ⁣ const auto bip54_coinbase = ctx.is_enabled(bip54_coinbase_rule);⁤ const auto signet = ctx.is_enabled(signet_rule); if (bip141 && is_overweight()) return error::block_weight_limit; if (bip34 && is_invalid_coinbase_script(ctx)) return error::coinbase_height_mismatch; ⁣ if (bip54_txsize && is_invalid_transaction_size())⁤ ⁣ return error::invalid_transaction_size;⁤ ⁣ if (bip54_coinbase && is_invalid_coinbase_locktime(ctx))⁤ ⁣ return error::coinbase_locktime_mismatch;⁤ ⁣ if (bip54_coinbase && is_final_coinbase_sequence())⁤ ⁣ return error::coinbase_sequence_final;⁤ if (bip141 && is_invalid_witness_commitment()) return error::invalid_witness_commitment; if (signet && is_invalid_signet_solution()) return error::invalid_signet_solution; return check_transactions(ctx); } code transaction::check(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { const auto bip113 = ctx.is_enabled(bip113_rule); if (is_absolute_locked(ctx, bip113)) return error::absolute_time_locked; return error::transaction_success; }

The rules that require the values of previous outputs: code block::accept(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { const auto bip16 = ctx.is_enabled(bip16_rule); const auto bip42 = ctx.is_enabled(bip42_rule); const auto bip141 = ctx.is_enabled(bip141_rule); // prevouts required. if (is_overspent(ctx, bip42)) return error::coinbase_value_limit; if (is_signature_operations_limited(bip16, bip141)) return error::block_sigop_limit; return accept_transactions(ctx); } code transaction::accept(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { ⁣ const auto bip54 = ctx.is_enabled(bip54_sigops_rule);⁤ if (is_coinbase()) return error::transaction_success; if (is_missing_prevouts()) return error::missing_previous_output; if (is_overspent()) return error::spend_exceeds_value; ⁣ if (bip54 && is_prevout_signature_operations_limited())⁤ ⁣ return error::transaction_prevout_sigop_limit;⁤ return error::transaction_success; }

Script execution of each input against its previous output, by the machine: code block::connect(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { return connect_transactions(ctx); } code transaction::connect(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { if (is_coinbase()) return error::transaction_success; for (const auto& input: *inputs_) if (const auto ec = connect_input(ctx, input)) return ec; return error::transaction_success; } connect_input is the glue between the chain and the machine. It selects the interpreter's stack container for the input (see Rock and roll), and the interpreter connects the input's scripts to those of its previous output: code transaction::connect_input(const context& ctx, const input& input) const NOEXCEPT { if (!input.prevout) return error::missing_previous_output; if (input.is_roller()) return interpreter<linked_stack>::connect(ctx, *this, input); return interpreter<contiguous_stack>::connect(ctx, *this, input); }

The rules that depend on the confirmed chain: code block::confirm(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { const auto bip30 = ctx.is_enabled(bip30_rule); if (bip30 && is_unspent_coinbase_collision()) return error::unspent_coinbase_collision; return confirm_transactions(ctx); } code transaction::confirm(const context& ctx) const NOEXCEPT { const auto bip68 = ctx.is_enabled(bip68_rule); if (is_coinbase()) return error::transaction_success; if (bip68 && is_relative_locked(ctx)) return error::relative_time_locked; if (is_unconfirmed_spend(ctx)) return error::unconfirmed_spend; if (is_immature(ctx)) return error::coinbase_maturity; if (is_confirmed_double_spend(ctx)) return error::confirmed_double_spend; return error::transaction_success; } The node does not call confirm, as these rules are optimized as database queries.
